title: Compile bug: Vulkan fails with a glslc lacking GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix since #24406 (fa_decode shaders built as coopmat unconditionally)
body:
### Git commit

`7fe450e19305b828c199d602c23a8337aaa1f03b` (v0.5.0). Also reproduces on master `6b790a9c29`.

### Operating systems

Linux, Other? (Please let us know in description)

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Since #24406, the Vulkan backend no longer builds when `glslc` does not support `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix`. The CMake feature test detects this correctly (`-- GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix not supported by glslc`), but two new shaders are compiled as coopmat variants unconditionally anyway, so `vulkan-shaders-gen` fails.

`vulkan-shaders-gen.cpp`:

```cpp
string_to_spv("fa_decode_ph1", "flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp", {}, true, true, false, false);
string_to_spv("fa_decode_ph2", "flash_attn_decode_phase_2.comp", {}, true, true, false, false);
```

These have no `#if defined(GGML_VULKAN_COOPMAT_GLSLC_SUPPORT)` guard. The pipeline creation in `ggml-vulkan.cpp` that references `fa_decode_ph1_cm1_data` / `fa_decode_ph2_cm1_data` (the Intel Xe `pipeline_xe_fa_decode_dual_phases` loop) isn't guarded either. Every other `_cm1` shader and pipeline sits behind that macro, so a coopmat-less glslc was a working configuration before this change. See #10785 / #11052 for the same class of break fixed earlier.

This affects any toolchain whose glslc predates `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix`. One example is the Android NDK's bundled glslc: NDK r28 (`28.2.13676358`) and r29 (`29.0.14206865`) both report `shaderc v2022.3`. Android cross-builds with `GGML_VULKAN=ON` commonly pass that glslc as `Vulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE`.

Minimal reproduction with the shader alone (same invocation as `vulkan-shaders-gen`):

```sh
$ANDROID_NDK/shader-tools/<host>/glslc -fshader-stage=compute --target-env=vulkan1.2 \
  ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp -o /dev/null
```

A likely fix is to guard both `string_to_spv` calls with `#if defined(GGML_VULKAN_COOPMAT_GLSLC_SUPPORT)`. The Xe dual-phase pipeline creation (or its registration) would get the same guard, so those devices fall back to the regular FA path when the shaders aren't built.

### First Bad Commit

4ceb17191 (vulkan: add Intel Xe flash attention optimization kernels (2/3, Xe-LPG Plus/Xe2/Xe3) (#24406))

### Compile command

```shell
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$ANDROID_NDK/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake \
  -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-28 \
  -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DVulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE=$ANDROID_NDK/shader-tools/linux-x86_64/glslc
cmake --build build --target ggml-vulkan
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
-- GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix not supported by glslc
...
FAILED: [code=1] .../flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp.cpp
glslc -fshader-stage=compute --target-env=vulkan1.2 .../vulkan-shaders/flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp -o .../fa_decode_ph1_cm1.spv ...
flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp:11: warning: '#extension' : extension not supported: GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix
flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp:115: error: 'coopmat' : undeclared identifier
flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp:115: error: '' :  syntax error, unexpected COMMA, expecting LEFT_PAREN
FAILED: [code=1] .../flash_attn_decode_phase_2.comp.cpp
flash_attn_decode_phase_2.comp:118: error: 'coopmat' : undeclared identifier
```

title: Misc. bug: prompt cache (--cache-ram) is dropped on wake from --sleep-idle-seconds, but kept in RAM while sleeping
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11064, commit a894dae93)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
router mode; the affected model preset resolves to (paths shortened):
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-A.gguf --jinja --parallel 4 --kv-unified --kv-unified-per-slot 49152 --ctx-size 196608 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --flash-attn auto --n-gpu-layers 99 --cache-idle-slots --cache-ram -1 --sleep-idle-seconds 900
minimal repro does not need any of that: llama-server -m <model>.gguf --cache-ram 8192 --sleep-idle-seconds 60
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Hardware: RTX 5090 32 GB, CUDA 13.4 build, Windows 11. Model: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid `qwen35`, Gated DeltaNet).

What happens

With `--cache-ram N` and `--sleep-idle-seconds S`:

1. `handle_sleeping_state(true)` calls `destroy()`, which resets the model, contexts and speculative state — but not `prompt_cache`, so the cache stays allocated for the whole sleep.
2. `handle_sleeping_state(false)` calls `load_model()`, and `load_model()` runs `prompt_cache = std::make_unique<server_prompt_cache>(params_base.cache_ram_mib, n_ctx);` — the previous cache and every saved state in it are dropped.

So the RAM is held while sleeping and then discarded, and every client that returns after an idle period re-processes its full prompt.

Steps to reproduce

1. `llama-server -m <model> --cache-ram 8192 --sleep-idle-seconds 60`
2. Send prompt A (~4k tokens), then a different prompt B (A goes to the prompt cache).
3. Send A again: only a few tokens are re-processed (restored from the cache).
4. Wait for `server is entering sleeping state`, send A again after the wake-up.

Expected: A is restored from the prompt cache. Actual: A is fully re-processed (see the log: 4 tokens processed before the sleep, 3974 and 3624 after the wake-up, for the same two prompts).

Impact

For long agent sessions (~100k tokens) every pause longer than the sleep timeout costs a full re-prefill (about a minute on an RTX 5090) on top of the model reload. For hybrid/recurrent models every cache entry also carries a large fixed state (~300 MiB here), so the memory held while sleeping is substantial.

Suggested fix

The saved states are host-side buffers from `llama_state_seq_get_data_ext`, valid for the same model with the same parameters, so `load_model()` could keep the existing cache, e.g. `if (!prompt_cache && params_base.cache_ram_mib != 0) prompt_cache = std::make_unique<...>(...);`. If keeping it is undesirable, releasing it in `destroy()` would at least free the RAM while sleeping.


### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. The same code is on master as of 2026-09-23 (load_model() creates prompt_cache; destroy() does not reset it).

### Relevant log output

before the sleep: after the first pass, the same two prompts come back from the cache (4 tokens processed)
[64129] 425.28.382.283 I slot print_timing: id  2 | task 38654 | prompt eval time =    1306.58 ms /  3896 tokens
[64129] 425.29.939.331 I slot print_timing: id  1 | task 38666 | prompt eval time =    1173.91 ms /  3493 tokens
[64129] 425.30.410.719 I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 38680 | prompt eval time =     105.51 ms /     4 tokens
[64129] 425.30.913.274 I slot print_timing: id  3 | task 38689 | prompt eval time =     110.84 ms /     4 tokens
[64129] 440.31.280.954 I srv  handle_sleep: server is entering sleeping state
[64129] 457.59.004.994 I srv  handle_sleep: server is exiting sleeping state
[64129] 457.59.005.208 I srv    load_model: loading model '.../Qwen3.8-27B-A.gguf'
[64129] 473.04.195.040 I srv  handle_sleep: server is entering sleeping state
[64129] 507.15.846.581 I srv  handle_sleep: server is exiting sleeping state
[64129] 507.15.846.797 I srv    load_model: loading model '.../Qwen3.8-27B-A.gguf'
# after the wake-up: the same two prompts are fully re-processed, then cached again
[64129] 507.21.193.959 I slot print_timing: id  3 | task 38706 | prompt eval time =    1292.45 ms /  3974 tokens
[64129] 507.22.750.721 I slot print_timing: id  2 | task 38719 | prompt eval time =    1192.68 ms /  3624 tokens
[64129] 507.23.251.425 I slot print_timing: id  1 | task 38734 | prompt eval time =     110.72 ms /     4 tokens

title: Eval bug: with -np 2 and --kv-unified, prompt processing drops 42-54% from the second long request onward (single GPU, sequential requests, no spill, no speculation)
body:
> **Update — known cause, previously recorded as not affecting prompt processing.**
> This is the unified-KV limitation in the CUDA/HIP flash-attention kernels: they skip
> only the **tails** of the KQ mask (`KV_max`), not all-`-INF` blocks in the interior, so
> a sequence pays for cells belonging to other (or released) sequences in the shared pool.
> Metal has interior block skipping; Vulkan got it in #17186. Extending it to CUDA was
> raised in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/14924#issuecomment-3683329376 and
> as far as I can tell has not landed.
>
> #19523 is the same root cause for **token generation** on Vulkan, and its reporter
> states *"And pp is not affected."* On HIP, prompt processing **is** affected, by 42-54%.
> Confirmed by A/B on `--kv-unified` (-41.8% unified vs -3.1% split, matched prompt) and
> reproduced with upstream's own `llama-batched-bench -kvu -tgs`: S_PP 885.55 -> 644.39
> across B=1,2,4 with `-kvu` versus 857.79 -> 833.20 with `-no-kvu` on stock master.
> Details: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/28495#issuecomment-5560879161
>
> Workaround: `--no-kv-unified` (also found independently by @alankila on Strix Halo).
> Note `-c` is then divided across slots.

### Name and Version

Reproduced on **stock master**, using the official release binary
(`llama-b10825-bin-win-rocm-10.0-x64.zip`), nothing local in it:

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10825, commit 9e0e22059)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
```

It was originally found on a local branch off b10665 (RDNA prefill tuning, a
chat-template fix, and the FA hunks from PR #28102). Stock master turns out to be
**worse** — -54% there versus -42% on the patched build — so those patches partially
mask the effect rather than causing it. Both sets of numbers are below.

### Operating systems

Windows (11 Pro, 10.0.26200)

### GGML backends

HIP (ROCm runtime 10.0.0 from TheRock, gfx1201)

### Hardware

**AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700** — a single discrete card, no second GPU, no iGPU in use
for compute:

- GPU: Radeon AI PRO R9700 (RDNA4, **gfx1201**, PCI device ID `0x7551`), 32 GiB VRAM
- Windows display driver 32.0.22042.14002 (2026-04-30)
- ROCm runtime 10.0.0 (TheRock Windows build for gfx120X)
- Host: 32 GiB system RAM

Note for anyone repeating this on the same card: the official `win-rocm` release zip
ships no rocBLAS/hipBLASLt, so `--list-devices` reports `(none)` straight out of the
archive. The runtime libraries have to be supplied alongside it before the GPU is
visible at all.

### Models

Qwen3.8-27B, UD-Q5_K_XL (locally requantised), `-fa on`, `-ctk f16 -ctv f16`.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With `-np 2`, the **first** long prompt after server start is processed at full speed.
**Every subsequent long prompt is ~42% slower**, and it never recovers for the lifetime
of the server. Requests are strictly **sequential** — one at a time, never concurrent.

This is not the known concurrency/speculation family of reports (see "What this is not"
below): it needs neither concurrent requests nor speculative decoding.

Method: to avoid accidentally changing more than one thing, each arm was produced by
reading the **command line of the running process** and substituting a single token,
rather than by rebuilding the command line. Same binary, same runtime, same model, same
context size, same corpus, same request order in every arm.

Load: 100 607-token prompt, `n_predict: 64`, `cache_prompt: false`, `ignore_eos: true`,
posted to `/completion` three times in a row.

#### Results on stock master (b10825)

| iter | `-np 2` | `-np 1` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 335.7 t/s | 323.5 t/s |
| 2 | **151.4** | 322.3 |
| 3 | **154.5** | 321.9 |
| change | **-54.0%** | **-0.5%** |

TTFT for the same 100 607-token prompt goes 299.7 s -> 664.6 s -> 651.1 s at `-np 2`,
and stays at 311.0 / 312.2 / 312.5 s at `-np 1`. Memory is flat in both arms
(dedicated 31 892 MiB / shared 434 MiB at `-np 2`; 31 292 / 490 MiB at `-np 1`),
sampled *during* the requests, so nothing is being evicted to host memory.

#### Results on the patched b10665 branch (where it was found)

| iter | `-np 2` | `-np 1` | `-np 2`, no speculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 690.6 t/s | 683.1 t/s | 752.0 t/s |
| 2 | **398.0** | 660.7 | **438.3** |
| 3 | **394.4** | 649.7 | **430.6** |
| change | **-42.4%** | -4.9% | **-42.7%** |

- `-np 1` does not collapse; the mild -4.9% drift over three iterations is normal here.
- Removing `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3` changes nothing about the
  collapse (-42.7% vs -42.4%), so speculative decoding is not involved.
- Generation speed is essentially unaffected — the loss is in prompt processing only.

A `-np 3` arm behaves the same way (644.3 / 365.4 / 367.5 t/s, -43.3%), i.e. the loss
does not scale with slot count — it looks like a threshold at "more than one slot".
I am reporting that arm with a caveat, though: at `-np 3` this model no longer fits and
the server loads with ~1 081 MiB spilled to host memory, so its absolute numbers are
contaminated and only the *shape* of the drop is meaningful.

#### It is not memory spill

Per-process GPU memory was sampled continuously *during* each request, not just after:

| arm | dedicated | shared (peak = end) |
|---|---|---|
| `-np 2` | 31 978 MiB | 436 MiB, flat across all 3 iterations |
| `-np 1` | 31 379 MiB | 491 MiB, flat |
| `-np 2`, no spec | 29 768 MiB | 264 MiB, flat |

Nothing is evicted to host memory, and the numbers do not move between the fast first
iteration and the slow later ones.

### What this is not

I checked the adjacent open reports before filing; this is a different failure:

- **#27544** (MTP n-max > 1 with -np > 1) — needs `draft-mtp` and genuinely concurrent
  sessions; degrades generation. Mine reproduces with speculation removed and with
  strictly sequential requests, and generation is fine.
- **#27117** (draft acceptance collapse under concurrent sequences) — scales with the
  number of concurrently *drafting* sequences. Only one request is ever in flight here.
- **#27428** (draft-mtp halves prompt processing) — multi-GPU layer split; the author
  reports single-GPU costs only ~3%. This is a single GPU.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown — not bisected. An older measurement on this machine with the same harness and
the same `-np 2` was flat (569.7 / 550.1 / 541.7 t/s), so conditions existed under which
it did not appear, but I cannot date the change and the `-np 1` control locates the cause
without needing to.

### Relevant log output

Command line for the `-np 2` arm (API key redacted, paths shortened):

```shell
llama-server.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL_V2.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf \
  --device ROCm0 -ngl 999 -c 163840 -fa on -np 2 --kv-unified --no-cache-idle-slots \
  --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 -t 6 --poll 0 --jinja \
  --chat-template-file <patched-template>.jinja \
  --temp 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --top-k 20 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 1.5 --repeat-penalty 1 \
  --cache-ram 0 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --api-key <REDACTED> \
  --no-mmproj-offload -ub 512 -b 1024 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3
```

The `-np 1` arm is the same line with `-np 2` replaced by `-np 1`; the no-speculation arm
is the same line with `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3` removed.
`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` is set in all arms.

title: draft-mtp speculative decoding not activating on Turing (sm_75) with hybrid SSM+attention model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
body:
## Environment

- llama.cpp build: 9626 (4988f6e86) and 9660 (7dad2f1a1)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 SUPER (Turing, sm_75, 4GB VRAM)
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)
- Driver: 595.71.05
- CUDA: 12.8

## Model

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-IQ1_M.gguf (hybrid SSM+attention architecture)
- arch: qwen35moe
- nextn_predict_layers: 1
- n_layer: 40, includes both attention and Mamba/SSM layers

## Command

./llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-IQ1_M.gguf \
  -c 65536 --flash-attn on \
  --ubatch-size 128 --batch-size 128 \
  -ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe 38 -np 1 \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --no-mmap -t 9 --jinja

## Problem

`draft-mtp` initializes without error but never actually activates.
The line `statistics draft-mtp` never appears in logs even after 800+ 
generated tokens. Performance is identical to running without MTP (~6 t/s).

## Key observation in logs

draft-mtp context initialization:
  - gpu_layers=-1, cache_k=f16, cache_v=f16, ctx_tgt=yes, ctx_dft=yes
  - graph splits = 2

Main context:
  - n_rs_seq = 2  (SSM recurrent state present)

Draft MTP context:
  - n_rs_seq = 0  (SSM recurrent state MISSING)

The draft MTP context has no recurrent state (n_rs_seq=0) while the 
main context has n_rs_seq=2. This may be the root cause — the draft 
context cannot properly handle the SSM/Mamba layers of this hybrid model.

## Comparison with working setup

Same model, same flags, same llama.cpp binary (build 9626):
- GTX 1050 (Pascal, sm_61) on laptop with integrated Intel GPU handling display
- draft-mtp works correctly: draft acceptance = 1.00, ~15 t/s
- `statistics draft-mtp` appears normally in logs

On GTX 1650 Super (Turing, sm_75):
- draft-mtp initializes but never activates
- `statistics draft-mtp` never appears
- Performance unchanged vs no MTP

## Hypothesis

The draft-mtp context does not correctly handle the SSM/Mamba recurrent 
state (n_rs_seq=0 in draft vs n_rs_seq=2 in main context) for hybrid 
attention+SSM architectures like Qwen3.6. This may be specific to or 
more visible on Turing (sm_75) but could affect other architectures too.

title: Docs: add backend selection guidance for different hardware configurations
body:
## Problem

The README and docs list supported backends (CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, CPU) but provide no guidance on which backend to use for a given hardware configuration. Users must dig through scattered issues and discussions to figure out e.g. whether to use HIP or Vulkan on an AMD RX 7900 XTX, or whether SYCL works on Intel Arc, or whether Metal or CPU is faster on an M-series Mac for a given model size.

## Suggested improvement

A structured backend recommendation table in `docs/backend-guide.md` (or similar) that maps:

- **GPU vendor + architecture** → **recommended backend(s)** + expected performance level
- **iGPU (Intel/AMD Apple)** → best backend
- **CPU-only** → which BLAS backend (OpenBLAS vs BLIS vs Accelerate vs oneAPI)

Each entry should note:
- Build flags needed (cmake -D...)
- Known limitations (e.g. Vulkan on older AMD cards, SYCL on specific Intel GPUs only)
- Quantization compatibility notes where backend matters

## Prior art

Discussions like #10982 (Metal vs Vulkan perf) and dozens of help threads show this info is repeatedly requested. Consolidating it would reduce maintainer burden from answering the same question.

## Value for maintainers

Fewer duplicate "which backend should I use?" issues.

title: GGML_ASSERT(id >= 0 && id < n_expert) with Gemma 4 26B-A4B + --n-cpu-moe on Vulkan
body:
# Eval bug: GGML_ASSERT(id >= 0 && id < n_expert) with Gemma 4 26B-A4B + `--n-cpu-moe` on Vulkan (crash) / corrupted output with reduced `--ubatch-size`

### Name and Version

```
version: 10042 (3f08ef2c5)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
```
Also reproduced on `version: 10038 (a320cbfcb)`.

Vulkan device line at load:
```
ggml_vulkan: 0 = Intel(R) Arc(TM) A770 Graphics (Intel Corporation) | uma: 0 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | fp4: 0 | warp size: 32 | shared memory: 49152 | int dot: 1 | matrix cores: none
```

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

Intel Core i5-13600K + Intel Arc A770 16GB (GPU driver 32.0.101.8861)

### Models

`lmstudio-community/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF` → `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` (MoE, A4B).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When offloading the routed experts to CPU with `--n-cpu-moe` (MoE-aware offload) on the **Vulkan** backend, Gemma 4 26B-A4B crashes **partway through a long prompt prefill** with:

```
GGML_ASSERT(id >= 0 && id < n_expert) failed   (ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:1615)
```

The model loads fine and prefill starts at a healthy rate (~130–160 t/s), then aborts once the prompt reaches roughly 10–20% of a 64K context. The exact crash point is data-dependent and differs between builds (see logs).

Minimal server repro:
```
llama-server \
  --model gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 65536 --n-gpu-layers 99 --n-cpu-moe 24 --flash-attn on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --jinja
```
Then send a chat request with a prompt of ~8K+ tokens. It crashes during prompt processing.

Also reproducible with `llama-bench` at depth:
```
llama-bench -m gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -ngl 99 -ncmoe 99 -p 512 -n 0 -d 65024
```
(pp512 @ depth 0 succeeds; the deep test aborts with the same assert.)

### What narrows it down

- **SYCL backend (Level Zero, same Arc A770) does NOT crash.** With `--n-cpu-moe` the same Gemma model prefills the full 64K without the assert (just slowly, ~52 t/s). So the fault appears specific to the **Vulkan MoE-offload path**, not to `--n-cpu-moe` in general.
- **GPT-OSS 20B (also MoE) with the same `--n-cpu-moe` on Vulkan does NOT crash** and completes 64K. So the trigger seems tied to Gemma 4's expert configuration rather than MoE offload universally.
- **Reducing `--ubatch-size` to 256 avoids the hard assert** — the prefill runs to the full 64K — **but the output becomes corrupted at high context** (garbled/misspelled tokens), while the same server produces clean text at low context. This strongly suggests the underlying cause is **wrong expert index selection under Vulkan MoE offload**: with `-ub 512` the bad index trips the assert; with `-ub 256` it silently selects wrong experts and produces corrupt output.

This looks related to the (closed) #18786, which reported the same assert for GPT-OSS 20B on Vulkan and was attributed to commit `2038101bd9b1` (#18166) / tag b7668. The GPT-OSS case now works, but Gemma 4 26B-A4B still fails on current `master`/release b10042.

### Relevant log output

Crash during prefill (b10038, `-ncmoe`, default ubatch):
```
slot print_timing: prompt processing, n_tokens = 4097, t = 31.59 s / 129.67 tokens per second
slot print_timing: prompt processing, n_tokens = 6145, t = 45.29 s / 135.68 tokens per second
D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:1615: GGML_ASSERT(id >= 0 && id < n_expert) failed
```

Crash on b10042 (same config), aborts a bit later:
```
slot print_timing: prompt processing, n_tokens = 8193, progress = 0.19, t = 53.95 s / 151.85 tokens per second
D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:1615: GGML_ASSERT(id >= 0 && id < n_expert) failed
```

Corrupted (non-crashing) output with `--ubatch-size 256` on b10042 at ~65K prompt tokens:
```
"LeIn frsi sopra riportate si sono ripetutute in modo identico per numer centosettantaantqu"
```
(same server, short prompt, correct output: "Il mare calmo riflette la luce del sole all'orizzonte...")

title: Eval bug: server -np 4 --kv-unified returns other requests' responses verbatim on integrated HIP GPU (gfx1151) — bisected to c7d87229
body:
## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

<details><summary>repro-crossover.py (needs httpx)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Repro: llama-server cross-request response mix-up under -np 4 --kv-unified.

Each round: (B) short "repeat exactly: <nonce>" request, (C) large-prompt
(~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce,
(D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain).
Every response must contain its OWN nonce and no nonce of an EARLIER request.

Usage: python3 repro-crossover.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 [--rounds 8]
Requires: pip install httpx
"""
import argparse, asyncio, json, random, string, sys, time
import httpx

FILLER = [
    "Quantized MoE models reach higher aggregate throughput under continuous batching.",
    "The KV cache grows linearly with context length and dominates memory for long prompts.",
    "Speculative decoding only pays off when the draft acceptance rate is high enough.",
    "A reranker only improves retrieval when the candidate set is broad enough.",
]

def big_prompt(seed, chars=30000):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    lines = [f"## Research block {seed}"]
    while sum(len(l) for l in lines) < chars:
        tag = "".join(rnd.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=8))
        lines.append(f"- [{tag}] {rnd.choice(FILLER)}")
    lines.append("\nSummarize the key points in 5 sentences.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

seen, violations, checks = [], [], 0

def check(phase, rnd, nonce, text):
    global checks
    checks += 1
    stem = nonce.rsplit("-", 1)[0]
    problems = []
    if nonce not in text and not (phase == "C" and stem in text):
        problems.append("own_nonce_missing")
    problems += [f"REPLAY_of:{o}" for o in seen if o != nonce and o in text]
    seen.append(nonce)
    if problems:
        violations.append((rnd, phase, problems, text[:120]))
        print(f"  VIOLATION R{rnd}/{phase}: {problems} got={text[:80]!r}", flush=True)

async def echo_req(c, url, model, nonce, stream=False):
    p = {"model": model, "max_tokens": 40, "temperature": 0,
         "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Repeat back exactly this code and nothing else: {nonce}"}]}
    if not stream:
        r = await c.post(f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", json=p)
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    p["stream"] = True
    out = []
    async with c.stream("POST", f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", json=p) as r:
        async for line in r.aiter_lines():
            if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]":
                try: out.append(json.loads(line[6:])["choices"][0]["delta"].get("content") or "")
                except Exception: pass
    return "".join(out)

async def synth_req(c, url, model, nonce, prompt):
    sysmsg = f"The FIRST line of your reply must be exactly `<!-- run:{nonce} -->`."
    r = await c.post(f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", json={
        "model": model, "max_tokens": 600,
        "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": sysmsg},
                     {"role": "user", "content": sysmsg + "\n\n" + prompt}]})
    return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

async def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8080")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="default")
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=8)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    ts = time.strftime("%H%M%S")
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=600.0) as c:
        for rnd in range(1, a.rounds + 1):
            bp = big_prompt("cachehit" if rnd % 2 == 0 else f"uniq-{ts}-{rnd}")
            nb = f"pb-{ts}-{rnd}-b"
            check("B", rnd, nb, await echo_req(c, a.url, a.model, nb))
            nc = f"pc-{ts}-{rnd}-c"
            check("C", rnd, nc, await synth_req(c, a.url, a.model, nc, bp))
            nd = [f"pd-{ts}-{rnd}-d{i}" for i in range(4)]
            res = await asyncio.gather(*[echo_req(c, a.url, a.model, n, stream=(i % 2 == 0))
                                         for i, n in enumerate(nd)], return_exceptions=True)
            for n, r in zip(nd, res):
                if not isinstance(r, Exception):
                    check("D", rnd, n, r)
            print(f"round {rnd} done — violations so far: {len(violations)}/{checks}", flush=True)
    print(f"\nRESULT: {len(violations)} violations / {checks} validated responses")
    return 1 if violations else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

```

</details>

Happy to run additional experiments on this hardware (it reproduces deterministically within 2–4 rounds).

title: CUDA / Volta (sm_70): certain inputs make Qwen3-Embedding-8B return an all-NaN embedding and then permanently wedge the server; CPU output is correct
body:
### Name and Version

Reproduced on `version: b10103 (da296d6e7)` (latest at time of writing), and also on `b6912` and the earliest Qwen3-Embedding-capable build (~July 2025). Present in every usable version → not a recent regression.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- GPU: NVIDIA **Tesla V100 SXM2 (Volta, sm_70)** — reproduced on two different cards (16 GB and 32 GB).
- CUDA toolkit: reproduced with **12.9.1** and **12.4**; driver **580.159.04**.
- Built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70`.
- OS: Debian 12.

### Models

**Qwen3-Embedding-8B** GGUF. Reproduced with **Q8_0, Q6_K, and f16**, from two independent conversions:
- https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B-GGUF
- https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/Qwen3-Embedding-8B-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Summary.** On a V100 (Volta, sm_70), `llama-server --embedding` with Qwen3-Embedding-8B returns an all-`null` (NaN) embedding for certain inputs. Once such an input is processed, the server is **wedged**: every subsequent request — including a trivial `"hello world"` — also returns an all-NaN vector, until the process is restarted. HTTP status is `200`, and the server log shows the request completing normally (`slot release ... truncated = 0`, no assert/error). The **same GGUF and input produce a correct vector on CPU** (`-ngl 0`). So this is a GPU-compute issue on Volta — not bad input, not the model math, not quantization.

**The trigger input.** A specific ~698-token chunk deterministically triggers it. It is valid UTF-8, ordinary source code + comments (mixed ASCII/Cyrillic); no control/zero-width/BOM characters; 697 tokens, all within vocab. Most inputs (incl. `"hello world"` and 64×3321-token = 212k-token batches) embed fine — the trigger is **content-specific**, not length/batch-related. The chunk is from a private codebase, so it is not pasted here; **I can share a minimal reproducer input privately** and prepare a redacted/synthetic equivalent, and I can run further diagnostics / `git bisect` on the hardware.

**Steps to reproduce.**
1. `llama-server -m Qwen3-Embedding-8B.Q8_0.gguf --embedding --pooling last -c 4096 -fa on -ngl 99` on a V100 (sm_70).
2. `POST /v1/embeddings` `{"input":"hello world"}` → valid vector.
3. `POST /v1/embeddings` `{"input":"<trigger chunk>"}` → all-null vector.
4. `POST /v1/embeddings` `{"input":"hello world"}` again → all-null (wedged until process restart).

**Isolation — what does NOT change the behavior (all still NaN + wedge):**

| Variable | Result |
|---|---|
| **CPU (`-ngl 0`)**, same GGUF + input | **CORRECT** valid vector → GPU path only |
| `-fa off` (flash-attn disabled) | still NaN |
| `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | still NaN |
| `--no-kv-unified` (separate per-slot KV) | still NaN, and a fresh independent request still wedges → not the KV cache |
| `--ctx-checkpoints 0` | still NaN |
| `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=1` (cuBLAS instead of quant MMQ) | still NaN → not the matmul kernel |
| Q8_0 / Q6_K / **f16 (no dequant)** | all NaN → not quantization |
| CUDA toolkit 12.9 → 12.4 | still NaN → not the toolkit version |
| llama.cpp b10103 / b6912 / ~Jul-2025 | all NaN → not a recent regression |

Because it survives separated/cleared per-slot KV and disabled checkpoints, yet a fresh trivial request is corrupted afterward, the NaN appears to land in **persistent GPU state** that every subsequent forward pass reads. `POST /slots/{id}?action=erase` returns `501` in embedding mode, so there is no runtime way to clear it — only a process restart.

**Expected:** a finite embedding on GPU matching the CPU result; and a single bad input must not corrupt subsequent independent requests.

### First Bad Commit

Not a regression — reproduced on the earliest Qwen3-Embedding-capable build (~July 2025), `b6912`, and current `b10103`. I'm happy to `git bisect` on the V100 if a maintainer suspects a specific range.

### Relevant log output

```
# Fresh server (V100, Q8_0, -fa on -ngl 99). null = count of JSON-null (NaN) values in the 4096-dim embedding.

POST /v1/embeddings {"input":"hello world"}   tokens=3    null=0/4096      first3=[0.0218, 0.0107, -0.0205]   OK
POST /v1/embeddings {"input":"<trigger>"}     tokens=698  null=4096/4096   first3=[null, null, null]          NaN
POST /v1/embeddings {"input":"hello world"}   tokens=3    null=4096/4096   first3=[null, null, null]          WEDGED
POST /v1/embeddings {"input":"test"}          tokens=2    null=4096/4096   first3=[null, null, null]          WEDGED

# Server log for the trigger request — completes "successfully", no error/assert:
slot   operator(): id  2 | task 2 | new prompt, n_ctx_slot = 4096, n_keep = 0, task.n_tokens = 698
slot   operator(): id  2 | task 2 | cached n_tokens = 0, memory_seq_rm [0, end)
slot      release: id  2 | task 2 | stop processing: n_tokens = 698, truncated = 0

# Same GGUF + same trigger input on CPU (-ngl 0): correct.
POST /v1/embeddings {"input":"<trigger>"}     tokens=698  null=0/4096      valid 4096-dim vector             OK
```

title: Eval bug:  Excessive compute buffer reservation in MTP draft context on ROCm HIP unnecessarily reduces fitted context size
body:

### Operating systems

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

CPU :  1th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-11400F
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6800

### Models

https://huggingface.co/GianniDPC/Qwen3.6-27B-IQ4_XS-pure-with-MTP-GGUF
qwen3.6-27b-IQ4_XS-pure-with-MTP-IQ4.gguf


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

 When enabling Native MTP (--spec-type draft-mtp) while using --fit-target , the MTP draft context is created with proposed max 262144 ctx reported by QWEN3.6 27B, instead of the fit-reduced context size. With 16GB GPU using an adequate small GGUF + reduced ctx like ~50K this eat some ~30k of the supposed available ctx. The issue is clearly visible launching the exact llama-serve script with Vulkan:

| Backend | MTP | Final `n_ctx` | Context [MiB] | Compute [MiB] | Context loss vs. no-MTP |
|---------|-----|--------------|---------------|---------------|------------------------|
|  ROCm    | ✅  | 19,456       | 544           | 37            | 72,448                 |
| ROCm    | ❌  | 91,904       | 245           | 37            | —                      |
| Vulkan  | ✅  | 69,120       | 544           | 38            | 40,960                 |
| Vulkan  | ❌  | 110,080      | 245           | 34            | —                      |

The "right amount" of ctx left available available with ROCm + MTP should be: ~55.8K tokens not 19,4k (~2.9x improvement on this test case). This is a huge difference for a 16GB GPU user, makes or brakes usability of such quant size.

That should be because:
 - CUDA/HIP (get_alloc_size) calls ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_get_alloc_size(), which accounts for F16 K/V copies proportional to  n_ctx. So flash attention workspace is counted upfront during fit, and over-allocating it directly reduces available context.

 - Vulkan (get_alloc_size) just returns ggml_nbytes(tensor) — the raw tensor size. Flash attention temp buffers are pre-allocated on-demand during execution, not during the fit phase. So the over-sized n_ctx doesn't inflate the memory estimate the same way.

## Result:
Compute memory and --fit-target margin are the same yet llama.cpp's  HIP is overestimating required GPU memory by roughly 800 MiB when I use MTP.


## How to reproduce

Launch llama-serve with and without --spec-type draft-mtp , I've posted next in "Relevant log output" such memory allocation reports of the same script ROCm vs vulkan from my RX 6800 RDNA2 GPU.

------------
Launch script:

llama-server  --device rocm0 \
 -m /home/eaman/lm/models/gianni/qwen3.6-27b-IQ4_XS-pure-with-MTP-IQ4.gguf \
        --host 0.0.0.0  -fa on --no-mmap --jinja --chat-template-file /home/eaman/lm/models/chat_template.jinja  --no-log-timestamps \
        -ctk q5_1 -ctv q5_1 \
        --temp 0.5 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0.05 \
        --presence-penalty 0.0 --repeat-penalty 1.0 \
        -b 1024 -ub 128 \
        --fit-target 60 \
        --spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod --spec-draft-p-min 0.82 --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
        --cache-type-k-draft q4_0 --cache-type-v-draft q4_0 \
        --spec-ngram-mod-n-match 24 --spec-ngram-mod-n-min 8 --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 32 \
        --ctx-checkpoints 128 --cache-ram 6000 -np 1 -ngl 99 -lv 4 --no-warmup \

title: Silent GTT fallback when context + MTP exceeds VRAM — no error at load, massive throughput collapse at runtime
body:
## Summary

With MTP speculative decoding enabled, loading a large context succeeds silently, but the first request causes ROCm to spill ~14.6 GB of buffers into GTT (system memory), collapsing prefill and decode throughput by 60%+ — with **no warning at load time**.

## Environment

- llama.cpp `11924d4c1` (also reproduced on `000547513`), HIP/ROCm backend
- AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT, 20 GB VRAM (20464 MiB total)
- `-np 1` single slot, flash attention on

## Model

Qwen3.6-27B (qwen35 architecture, 65 layers, 17 KV layers, embedded nextn/MTP head), IQ4_XS (~14.1 GB).

## Reproduction

Same model, same 74.7K-token actual context (KV usage identical), only `-c` differs:

```
llama-server -m model.gguf -ngl 99 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -fa on -fit off \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 -c <131072|196608>
```

| Config | Decode | Prefill | Load-time VRAM+GTT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072` + MTP | 42-46 tok/s (MTP speedup 3.0x) | 449 tok/s | 18.60 GB VRAM + 0.43 GB GTT (1.4 GB headroom) |
| `-c 196608` + MTP | **18 tok/s (speedup 1.27x)** | **303 tok/s** | 19.95 GB VRAM + 0.62 GB GTT (**already over**) |
| `-c 131072` no MTP | 14.2 tok/s | 449 tok/s | — |
| `-c 196608` no MTP | 14.1 tok/s | 470 tok/s | — |

## Evidence: GTT spill during request

Monitoring `/sys/class/drm/card1/device/mem_info_gtt_used` while the request runs (196K + MTP):

```
11:15:12  GTT 0.59 GB   (request starts, prefill)
11:15:52  GTT 14.65 GB  ← prefill middle: buffers moved to system memory
11:16:12  GTT 14.04 GB      (VRAM simultaneously dropped to 19.28 GB)
11:16:32  GTT 0.47 GB   (prefill done)
```

For comparison, `-c 131072` + MTP keeps GTT flat at 0.43 GB for the whole request.

Without MTP, `-c 196608` behaves identically to `-c 131072` (14.1 vs 14.2 tok/s) — the window itself is not the problem. MTP's extra footprint (draft context + runtime buffers) pushes the total requirement past the VRAM line.

## Expected behavior

The load phase should validate against **runtime peak memory** (including compute-graph buffers / FA workspace), not just static weight+KV usage, and either refuse to start or emit a clear warning when GTT fallback will occur. A "successful" load followed by an unwarned 3x throughput collapse is a footgun — users cannot tell whether their config actually fits.

title: speculative-simple: dflash drafters draft without target features (silent low acceptance)
body:
Two related problems when using dflash-family drafters with `llama-speculative-simple`:

1. The draft context was created without `ctx_other` and not null-checked, which crashes on drafters that borrow the target's token embeddings / output head (e.g. the deepseek-ai dspark checkpoints). Fixed by #26883.

2. Even with `ctx_other` wired, the example evals the prompt with plain `llama_decode` on both contexts, so the dflash encoder never receives the target-layer features for the prompt. The drafter then drafts without its conditioning input and acceptance drops to single digits, where the same model pair through llama-server reaches its normal 40-50%. This failure is silent, so it is easy to mistake for a drafter or quantization problem (it cost us a while).

If speculative-simple is meant to stay a minimal example for classic drafters, the warning added in #26883 may be enough. Otherwise the prompt pass needs to go through the framework's speculative path so target-layer extraction is armed before the target prompt eval and the encoder is fed before the first draft.

title: Blackwell discrete GPUs (RTX 5080/5070Ti) misclassified as iGPU — breaks multi-GPU tensor split on Linux
body:
## Summary

On Linux with dual NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (RTX 5080 + RTX 5070 Ti, CUDA 13.3), `llama-server` silently ignores the second GPU and loads the entire model onto GPU0, causing an OOM when the model exceeds single-GPU VRAM.

## Root Cause

In `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, `ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_type()` classifies a device as `GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_IGPU` when `prop.integrated > 0`:

\`\`\`cpp
return prop.integrated
    ? GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_IGPU
    : GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU;
\`\`\`

Blackwell GPUs report `prop.integrated > 0` because they support hardware-level unified memory access (a new Blackwell feature). This is not the same as being a true integrated GPU.

This causes two cascading bugs:

1. **Both GPUs classified as IGPU** — `llama_prepare_model_devices()` in `src/llama.cpp` only ever adds the *first* iGPU to the device list, so CUDA1 is silently dropped and `--tensor-split` has no effect.
2. **Wrong memory reporting** — the UMA memory path reads system RAM (~77 GB on a 96 GB system) instead of actual VRAM (15.8 GB), causing `common_params_fit_impl` to believe a single GPU has enough memory for the entire model.

## Symptoms

- `llama_prepare_model_devices: using device CUDA0` — only one GPU logged even with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0,1"` and `--tensor-split`
- All layers assigned to CUDA0 in verbose output
- `ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating ~16 GiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory`
- GPU free memory reported as ~77 GiB (system RAM) instead of ~15.8 GiB (actual VRAM)

## Fix

Guard the iGPU classification with a VRAM threshold. True iGPUs (Intel, AMD APU) have little or no dedicated VRAM; discrete Blackwell GPUs have ≥16 GB:

\`\`\`cpp
// In ggml_backend_cuda_device_get_type():
return (prop.integrated && prop.totalGlobalMem < (size_t)4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
    ? GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_IGPU
    : GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU;
\`\`\`

The same guard should be applied to the UMA memory reporting path (`is_uma` check in the memory query function) to fix the inflated free-memory figures.

## Environment

- GPUs: RTX 5080 (16 GB) + RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB) — Blackwell GB20x
- CUDA: 13.3 / nvcc 13.3
- OS: Pop!_OS 22.04 (Linux 7.0.11)
- llama.cpp build: 10367 (704485942)
- sm_120 (Blackwell native)

## Verified

After applying the fix above and rebuilding, both GPUs appear in `llama_prepare_model_devices`, layers split correctly across CUDA0 and CUDA1, and a 17 GB model loads successfully across 2×16 GB GPUs.

title: Misc. bug: EAGLE3 draft model fails to load in speculative pairing with 'invalid vector subscript' on Windows (standalone load works)
body:
### Git commit

Release binaries b10354 and b10358 (`llama-*-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip`), Windows x64

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

RTX 5080 16GB (compute 12.0) · Intel Core Ultra 7 265KF · Windows 11

### Models

- Target: `ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF` → `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf`
- Draft: same repo → `eagle3-gpt-oss-20b-BF16.gguf` AND `eagle3-gpt-oss-20b-Q8_0.gguf` (both affected)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Loading an EAGLE3 draft model via `llama-server` speculative pairing fails with `llama_model_load: error loading model: invalid vector subscript` (MSVC STL checked `std::vector` access). The same draft GGUF loads fine standalone.

```
llama-server -m gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf --port 8099 -ngl 99 -fa on -c 8192 --no-webui ^
  -md eagle3-gpt-oss-20b-BF16.gguf --spec-type draft-eagle3
```

Evidence matrix (all on the same machine, same files):

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `llama-cli -m eagle3-...-BF16.gguf -ngl 0` (standalone) | loads OK |
| `llama-cli -m eagle3-...-BF16.gguf -ngl 99` (standalone) | loads OK |
| server pairing, defaults (fit on), b10354 & b10358, both quants | **crash** |
| server pairing `--fit off -c 8192` (f16 KV) | loaded once — spec decode confirmed working (`draft_n 380, accepted 128`) |
| server pairing `--fit off` + `-ncmoe 8` | **crash** |
| server pairing `--fit off -c 4096` (±`-ctk/-ctv q8_0`, ±`-ngld 99`, ± freed VRAM) | **crash** |

So the failure is confined to the draft-pairing load path (`common_speculative_init_result` → `llama_model_load_from_file`) and appears state-dependent rather than strictly config-dependent (1 success in 6 server attempts; standalone never fails). Draft GGUF metadata looks sane: arch `eagle3`, block_count 1, `eagle3.target_layers=[2,12,21]`, d2t 64000→201088.

Possibly related: #24795 (MTP draft, same error string, regression), #22337.

title: Eval bug: native MTP reserves a separate CUDA compute arena and OOMs; shared gallocr fixes it
body:
### Name and Version

llama-server --version

version: 10194 (e1a1abb78)
built with GNU 11.5.0 for Linux x86_64

git commit:
e1a1abb78746c025f5e9039f590e37ccdb758ae7

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X
RAM: 128 GB DDR4-3200
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 Founders Edition, 24 GB VRAM
NVIDIA driver: 550.163.01
CUDA: 12.4
Compute capability: 8.9

### Models

Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
Quantization: UD-Q4_K_XL

GGUF metadata:
general.architecture = qwen35
qwen35.block_count = 65
qwen35.context_length = 262144
qwen35.embedding_length = 5120
qwen35.feed_forward_length = 17408
qwen35.attention.head_count = 24
qwen35.attention.head_count_kv = 4
qwen35.nextn_predict_layers = 1

Multimodal projector:
mmproj-BF16.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I reproduced a native MTP VRAM allocation problem on a clean llama.cpp b10194 build.

Hardware:
- RTX 4090 24 GB
- Ryzen 9 5950X
- 128 GB RAM
- CUDA 12.4
- Linux

Model:
Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf

Configuration:
- context: 196608
- KV cache: q4_0 / q4_0
- parallel: 1
- native `draft-mtp`
- `--spec-draft-n-max 2`
- all model/MTP layers on GPU

With clean b10194, the target context loads, but creation of the native MTP draft context fails because it tries to reserve an additional CUDA compute buffer.

Baseline A0:

`n_ubatch = 512`

The MTP context attempts:

`allocating 1040.28 MiB on device 0`

and fails with:

`cudaMalloc failed: out of memory`
`failed to allocate compute pp buffers`
`failed to create MTP context`

I then made one isolated change: cap only the MTP compute micro-batch from 512 to 32 while keeping `n_batch` unchanged.

A1:

`n_batch=2048 n_ubatch=512->32`

This reduces the requested MTP compute allocation to:

`785.27 MiB`

but it still fails with CUDA OOM.

I then tested a proof-of-concept where the target and MTP contexts keep independent backend schedulers, but share the backing ggml gallocr / CUDA compute arena.

I initially tried sharing the entire scheduler, but that is not valid and caused a backend identity assertion. The working implementation shares only the backing allocator while keeping both schedulers independent.

With the shared-gallocr implementation:

- model loads successfully
- native MTP remains on GPU
- context remains 196608
- KV remains q4_0
- llama-server process VRAM after generation: 22038 MiB
- generation: 61.80 tokens/s
- draft tokens generated: 152
- draft tokens accepted: 96
- draft acceptance: 63.16%
- mean draft length: 2.26
- graphs reused: 1

The proof-of-concept does not share scheduler state or backend scheduling decisions between the target and MTP contexts. Each context retains its own scheduler; only the backing graph allocator / compute workspace is shared.

The relevant runtime messages are:

`Q38F_SHARED_GALLOC: MTP eligible; target/MTP schedulers stay independent`

`sched_reserve: Q38F_SHARED_GALLOC sharing target compute arena`

followed by:

`model loaded`

`listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`

This suggests that for sequential target/MTP execution (`--parallel 1`), reserving independent backing compute arenas is unnecessarily expensive. The schedulers can remain independent while sharing the backing graph allocator / compute workspace.

I am presenting the shared-gallocr implementation as a proof of the allocation issue, not as a claim that this is necessarily the final upstream design.

I created a standalone proof-of-concept patch against clean b10194. It applies cleanly to a second detached b10194 worktree using `git apply --check`.

Reproduction command:

    build/bin/llama-server \
      -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
      --mmproj mmproj-BF16.gguf \
      --no-mmproj-offload \
      -ngl 999 \
      -c 196608 \
      --cache-type-k q4_0 \
      --cache-type-v q4_0 \
      --flash-attn on \
      --parallel 1 \
      --spec-type draft-mtp \
      --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
      --spec-draft-type-k q4_0 \
      --spec-draft-type-v q4_0 \
      --spec-draft-ngl all \
      --metrics

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected.

The issue was reproduced on a clean b10194 checkout:

e1a1abb78746c025f5e9039f590e37ccdb758ae7

I am not claiming that this commit introduced the behavior.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Clean b10194 - baseline MTP OOM</summary>

```console
common_speculative_init_result: creating MTP draft context against the target model
ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 1040.28 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 1090814080
graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers
llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate compute pp buffers
common_speculative_init_result: failed to create MTP context
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>MTP n_ubatch=32 - still OOM</summary>

```console

ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 785.27 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 823411840
graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers
common_speculative_init_result: failed to create MTP context

title: spec: greedy output diverges from non-speculative baseline under batched verification on CUDA (deterministic numerics; draft-simple alone reproduces, DFlash2 amplifies)
body:
## Summary

With speculative decoding enabled (`temp 0`, fixed seed, otherwise identical settings), greedy output diverges from the identical non-speculative run. The divergence is **deterministic** (reruns are byte-identical) and is classified as **CUDA numerical divergence under batched speculative verification**, not a logic bug: the plain `draft-simple` path — which exercises batched verification with none of the DFlash2 code — reproduces it on one workload, while the DFlash2 path amplifies it (diverges on both workloads tested, and earlier).

Outputs remain coherent; this is a bit-exactness concern only, and speculative acceptance is unaffected. No fix is claimed here — this is a documentation/confirmation request.

## Environment

- llama.cpp at PR #27342 head: `5ecbe1ac17ec0484c5b44af0bd580cdc9c428ed4` (local build, MSVC 19.44, CUDA 12.4, sm_86)
- OS: Windows 11 x86_64
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3090 Ti 24 GB
- Target: `empero-ai/Qwen3.8-27B-Ridge-GGUF` `Qwen3.8-27B-Ridge-3.7bpw.gguf` (IQ2_M)
- Draft: `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF` `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf` (1,143,006,752 bytes; SHA-256 `18a380efc9b7ed8d88677fc895f5c11ae170653434ee378f7348f715c14d0594`)

## Repro (llama-cli, 6 runs)

Baseline (`--spec-type none`):

```
llama-cli -m <target> -ngl 999 --flash-attn on -c 8192 \
  --cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 -b 256 -ub 128 -t 8 \
  --temp 0 -s 42 --no-display-prompt -no-cnv -st \
  -n 256 -f prompt_short.txt < nul
```

Speculative variants add:

```
  -md <draft> --spec-draft-ngl 999 --spec-draft-n-max 7 --spec-draft-p-min 0 \
  --spec-type draft-simple        # or draft-dflash
```

Run the same with `-n 512 -f prompt_coding.txt`. Note: `--draft-model` is **not** a valid flag in this build; use `-md` (cli) / `--spec-draft-model` (server).

## Results (token-level, same-vocab `llama-tokenize`)

| workload | none vs draft-simple | none vs draft-dflash |
|---|---|---|
| short (n=256) | diverge at gen-token ~109 | diverge at gen-token ~49 |
| coding (n=512) | **identical 512/512** | diverge at gen-token ~372 |

Stripped-output MD5 (static banner/prompt-echo removed; generation content only):

| run | short | coding |
|---|---|---|
| none | `db0b78ede21fcb32543217e5cbfd437f` (1330 B) | `1d69d9619a1bde9249dac21e6fccaf99` (2482 B) |
| draft-simple | `c55e97dec9b537272f72dc578e1f00dc` (1346 B) | `1d69d9619a1bde9249dac21e6fccaf99` (2482 B) — **= none** |
| draft-dflash | `25dfca084f4cec36bc8f71f5eaa8da24` (1401 B) | `24d531f596c8aa41c1119ea01bd824d7` (2459 B) |

Reruns are byte-identical (determinism confirmed).

Example near-tie flips (short workload): `" storage of information."` vs `", recall, forgetting"`; `". Too many"` vs `"syllables. Too"`. Coding workload: digit flip `"1, 2"` vs `"8, 4"` in generated code.

## Analysis

- Batched verification alone (`draft-simple`, no DFlash hooks) perturbs CUDA target logits at near-ties: it diverges on the short workload yet is byte-identical on coding → **near-tie dependent, not systematic**.
- `draft-dflash` diverges on both workloads and earlier: DFlash2's extraction graph (`llama_set_embeddings_layer_inp` graph-output marking) amplifies the numeric shift but is **not the sole cause** (proven by the `draft-simple` divergence).
- Deterministic across reruns → consistent with CUDA fp-non-associativity in the batched verification decode (e.g. n_max=7 draft batch in one flash-attn batch vs sequential target decode) and/or graph-extraction side effects.
- Supporting data point: z-lab's Metal validation of DFlash2 achieved byte-identical greedy output (see z-lab/llama.cpp-fork#1), suggesting a platform-numeric component.

## Questions

1. Is bit-exact greedy output expected to be preserved under batched speculative verification on CUDA? (MTP presumably shows the same class of divergence.)
2. Is there a supported way to force the sequential target-decode path during verification, for bit-exact comparisons?
3. If this is accepted as generic numerics, it may be worth a short note in PR #27342 so downstream users don't mistake it for output corruption.

Cross-links: PR #27342 (DFlash2), companion issue [mtmd vision position-gap](#27408), z-lab/llama.cpp-fork#1 (Metal byte-identical validation).

title: Eval bug: qwen35moe (hybrid recurrent/attention) models produce empty generation when prompt exceeds ~16K tokens via llama-server (Metal)
body:
### Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 0.1.1-dev (build 10470, commit 34af94cd9)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

Also tested with:

```
version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10502, commit 0adcc3bb5)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

and self-built master:

```
version: 0.1.2-dev (build 1, commit dc72703)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple M4 (Mac mini, 16 GB unified memory)

### Models

- [vcruz305/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/vcruz305/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF) 

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Hybrid-attention (`qwen35moe`) models generate an **empty completion through `llama-server` when the prompt exceeds a context-dependent threshold (~16.5K with `-c 65536`, ~18-19K with `-c 32768`)**. The response has `predicted_n = 1`, empty `content`, and `eval time = 0.00 ms`. The same setup works fine below the threshold.

**Key refinement discovered while preparing this report (2026-08-20):**

1. **The threshold depends on `-c` (context size)**, not just prompt length:
   - With `-c 65536`: 16.5K prompt tokens fails consistently (3/3 trials), 15.4K works
   - With `-c 32768`: 16.5K works (2/2), 17.6K is **intermittent** (2 pass / 2 fail), 19.8K fails consistently (4/4)
   - This is NOT flash-attn related: reproduced with `--flash-attn on` and off, identical results
2. **There is randomness near the threshold**: the same request at 17.6K (`-c 32768`) succeeded on one attempt and failed on the next, with no code change between them. The failure looks like an uninitialized/stale recurrent-state restore that sometimes happens to work.
3. **Not all DeltaNet/recurrent architectures are affected**: `Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Thinking` (GGUF, `mellum` arch, 28 layers with fused Gated Delta Net) generates **normally up to 48K prompt tokens** on the same build (`-c 65536`). This isolates the bug to the **`qwen35moe` hybrid attention implementation** (mixed KV-attention + DeltaNet layers), not the DeltaNet operator itself.

The native context length of these models is 262K, so being effectively hard-capped at ~16-19K via the server is a severe practical limitation.

Reproduction (server):

```
llama-server -m <model>.gguf \
  -c 65536 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ngl 99 -np 1 --no-warmup -ub 512 \
  --port 8080
```

Send a chat completion request whose prompt is >= ~16.5K tokens, `max_tokens > 1`.

Boundary sweep results (`-c 65536`, identical across b10470 / dc72703 / b10502):

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 111 (short) | OK, 12 tokens generated |
| 15401 | OK, 12 tokens generated |
| 16501 | FAIL - predicted_n=1, empty content, eval 0.00 ms |
| 17601 | FAIL - empty |
| 19801 | FAIL - empty |
| 23981 | FAIL - empty |

Same sweep with `-c 32768` (b10502, no flash-attn):

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 15401 | OK |
| 16501 | OK (2/2) |
| 17601 | **INTERMITTENT (2 pass / 2 fail)** |
| 19801 | FAIL (4/4) |
| 23981 | FAIL |

Control: `Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Thinking-MXFP4_MOE.gguf` (mellum arch, fused Gated Delta Net) with `-c 65536`:

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 15401 / 16501 / 17601 / 19801 / 23981 / 30K / 48K | **ALL OK** (12 tokens generated) |

Prefill completes normally and takes the expected time (24K-token prefill ~ 92 s); the failure happens before the first generated token. No crash, no log errors - just an immediate empty completion.

Builds tested, all reproduce:
- Homebrew `llama.cpp` b10470 (commit `34af94cd9`)
- Self-built master `dc72703` (2026-08-19, `GGML_METAL=ON`)
- Official prebuilt b10502 (commit `0adcc3bb5`)
- Earlier: b10450, b10488, PrismML b9599 (also affected)

What has been ruled out:
- **Not memory/swap**: with `-c 65536 -ngl 99` the model loads and runs with zero swap (RSS ~5-11 GiB depending on build; the difference is due to Metal unified-memory mapping changes between builds)
- **Not KV quantization**: reproduced with both f16 and q4_0 KV caches
- **Not flash-attn related**
- **Not the compute graph**: `llama-bench` with a pure graph `pp20000+tg128` succeeds (268.93 t/s) - the graph layer is fine. The bug is in the **server's prompt-cache / context-checkpoint restore path for recurrent layers**
- **Not specific to one build or quant**: 4+ builds and 3 models all reproduce

Workarounds tried (all ineffective):
- `--ctx-checkpoints 0 --cache-reuse 0` - still empty output
- `--cache-ram 0` (disables prompt cache entirely) - still empty output
- `cache_prompt=false` per request - still empty output

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

Server startup (b10502, truncated):

```console
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-IQ2_XXS.gguf -c 65536 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ngl 99 -np 1 --no-warmup -ub 512 --port 8093
...
llama_model_load: loading model
...
server is listening on http://127.0.0.1:8093 - starting the main loop
```

Request at 16.5K prompt tokens - empty completion:

```console
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8093/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<16.5K token prompt>"}],"max_tokens":12}'
{"choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":""},"finish_reason":"stop"}], ...}
```

Server timing line for the failing request:

```console
slot print_timing: id  0 | task NNNN | prompt eval time = 55328.02 ms / 16501 tokens (3.35 ms per token, 298 tokens per second)
slot print_timing: id  0 | task NNNN |        eval time =      0.00 ms /     1 tokens

```

</details>

title: Misc. bug: llama-finetune crashes with 'failed to allocate buffer of size 18446744073709547520' before training starts (all model precisions)
body:
### Name and Version

```console
$ build/bin/Release/llama-cli.exe --version
version: 0.2.0-dev (build 10603, commit c060ca974)
built with MSVC 19.44.35228.0 for x64
```

Also reproduced at commit `39c59ed00` (build b10609). The affected files (`src/llama-context.cpp`, `ggml/src/ggml-opt.cpp`, `examples/training/finetune.cpp`) are unchanged between `c060ca974` and current upstream master (`c1c766da5`), so master is affected too.

### Operating systems

- [x] Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

- [x] libllama (core library)
- [x] Other (llama-finetune — `examples/training/finetune.cpp`, new `llama_opt`-based training path)

### Command line

```shell
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 -DGGML_CUDA=OFF -DGGML_VULKAN=OFF
cmake --build build --config Release --parallel

build\bin\Release\llama-finetune.exe -m <model> -f train.txt -o out.gguf -c 512 -lr 1e-4 -epochs 1 -opt adamw -t 16
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-finetune` crashes during the **first training-graph allocation**, before any epoch runs, with:

```
E ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: failed to allocate buffer of size 18446744073709547520
E alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate CPU buffer of size 18446744073709547520
```

`18446744073709547520 == 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF000 == -4096` (as int64). The requested size is a wrapped-around negative value, so some tensor in the training graph gets an invalid size.

Reproduced with three models / three weight precisions (`train.txt` is a small chat-format text file):

| model | precision | source |
|---|---|---|
| `stories260K.gguf` | F32 | https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models/resolve/main/tinyllamas/stories260K.gguf |
| `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-f16.gguf` | F16 | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF |
| `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-q4_k_m.gguf` | Q4_K_M | same repo |

Changing `-c`, `-b`, `-ub` does not affect the failure (always size `-4096`). `test-opt.exe` passes (`46/46 tests`, `2/2 backend*optimizer`) — the ggml opt engine itself works. The crash happens right after model warmup, at the first `ggml_backend_sched_alloc_graph()` call inside `ggml_opt_alloc()` (`ggml/src/ggml-opt.cpp`), invoked from `llama_context::opt_epoch_iter` (`src/llama-context.cpp`).

### First Bad Commit

Unknown. The `llama_opt`-based finetune is new (`finetune.cpp` was rewritten from the previous `--train-data` interface; `llama_context::opt_init` even carries a `// FIXME` marker). There is currently no CI or test coverage for `llama-finetune` (no finetune invocations in `.github/workflows/` or `tests/`).

title: Eval bug: Windows HIP gfx1201: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 loads, then first MUL_MAT fails with ROCm invalid argument
body:
### Name and Version

- llama.cpp release: `b10566`
- version: `0.2.0-dev`
- commit: `bb4caa754`

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB
- GPU architecture: `gfx1201`
- AMD driver: `32.0.31035.1003`
- System RAM: ~31.6 GiB

### Models

`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce


### ROCm runtime

Official ROCm `7.14.0` Windows runtime for `gfx1201`.

### Model

`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`

Original checkpoint:
- 3 safetensors shards
- ~21.816 GiB

Converted with the official llama.cpp converter to:

- file type: `MOSTLY_NVFP4`
- parameters: `34,660,672,370`
- GGUF size: ~20.638 GiB

NVFP4 expert weights were repacked directly rather than requantized.
The remaining FP8 tensors were represented as BF16 by the converter.

### Problem

The model loads successfully.

`llama-server` correctly detects:

```text
AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
gfx1201
```

The API becomes ready and VRAM usage after loading is approximately:

```text
14.946 GiB
```

However, the first real inference request terminates the backend on the first compute:

```text
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: MUL_MAT failed
ROCm error: invalid argument
ggml-cuda.cu:2408
```

There is no Windows TDR and no driver reset.

The llama.cpp process exits because of the fatal HIP error.

### Reproduction summary

1. Use official Windows HIP llama.cpp `b10566` (`bb4caa754`).
2. Use official ROCm 7.14 runtime for `gfx1201`.
3. Convert `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` with the official converter to `MOSTLY_NVFP4` GGUF.
4. Start `llama-server` using the HIP backend and normal GPU offload / auto-fit.
5. Wait until the model is loaded and the API becomes ready.
6. Send the first normal generation request.
7. Backend exits at `MUL_MAT` with `ROCm error: invalid argument`.

### Additional observations

```text
API_ready=YES
GPU=gfx1201
VRAM_after_load≈14.946 GiB
TDR=NO
driver_reset=NO
```

Repeated generation and `llama-bench` were intentionally not run after the first fatal HIP failure.

The same source Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 checkpoint is confirmed to run end-to-end on the same RX 9070 XT through another Windows ROCm inference path, so the checkpoint and GPU are capable of inference on this system.

This may be related in broad area to #23934, which also involves HIP `ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat` failures. The failure here is different, however:

- this system is Windows / `gfx1201`;
- model is Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4;
- error is `ROCm error: invalid argument`;
- model load and API initialization both succeed before the first real compute.

title: Eval bug: Possible regression: DSV4 CUDA compute buffer size
body:
### Name and Version

[b10615](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10615), [Windows x64 (CUDA 13)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b10615/llama-b10615-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip) - [CUDA 13.3 DLLs](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b10615/cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip)

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Ryzen 5950x
RTX 4090
Windows 10 22H2

### Models

[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-3.86bpw-Q3_K.gguf](https://huggingface.co/ddh0/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/blob/main/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-3.86bpw-Q3_K.gguf)


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

DeepSeek V4 Flash has an increase in CUDA compute buffer size, which could be a regression. The problem is absent in [b10567](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10567), first appeared in [b10568](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10568) and still present in [b10615](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10615), which is the latest release at the moment of opening this issue. To reproduce the problem, run DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 and compare the CUDA compute buffer size between the two. In my particular case, CUDA0 compute buffer size increased from 2366.28 MiB to 2570.28 MiB

### First Bad Commit

I don't know the exact commit, but it's a part of [b10568](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10568), [Windows x64 (CUDA 13)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b10568/llama-b10568-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip) - [CUDA 13.3 DLLs](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b10568/cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip)

title: Misc. bug: llama-server (HIP/ROCm build) spins 2 threads at 100% CPU when idle in router mode (WSL2)
body:
### Name and Version

llama.cpp commit `030ebb558a5820b444a8f836ed5cdd46c9b4bd7a` (2026-08-11), built with GNU 11.4.0 for Linux x86_64, `GGML_HIP=ON` (ROCm), no CUDA.

### Operating systems

- [x] Windows (WSL2: Windows 11 10.0.26200, WSL 2.7.11.0, kernel 6.18.33.2, Ubuntu-22.04)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

- [x] llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server --models-preset <models.ini> --host 0.0.0.0 --port 12347 -ngl 99 --models-max 2 --sleep-idle-seconds 300
```

Environment: `HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION=1`, `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0`, `HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0`.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` built with the HIP/ROCm backend spins **2 threads at ~100% CPU each, continuously, while completely idle** in router mode on WSL2 with an AMD GPU (Radeon RX 7900 XTX, paravirtualized via dxg).

Reproduction:

1. Start llama-server in router mode: `--models-preset <ini> --host 0.0.0.0 --port 12347 -ngl 99 --models-max 2 --sleep-idle-seconds 300`.
2. Do not load any model (all models unloaded, no child processes).
3. Observe: two threads of the process are each pinned at ~100% CPU from process start, continuously, with zero HTTP traffic.

Evidence:

- `top -H`: TID 1905 `R` 99.9%, TID 1906 `R` 99.9%, `TIME+` identical and growing; main thread blocked in `futex_do_wait`.
- `/proc/<tid>/wchan` of the two spinning threads = 0 (pure user-space busy loop, no kernel blocking).
- No iowait (`wa=0`), no memory pressure (17 GB free, no swap).
- Not traffic-related: persists with zero requests for minutes.
- Not model-state-related: occurs with all models unloaded AND after a model enters sleeping state.
- `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` (fix for idle GPU load, PR #24237) has no effect on this CPU spin.

Impact:

- 2 of 8 cores busy-waiting constantly while idle (~25% total CPU wasted).
- The CUDA equivalent busy-wait is addressed by `GGML_CUDA_BLOCKING_SYNC` (PR #26487); no HIP/ROCm equivalent found.
- Related discussion: #22238 (100% CPU single core usage while everything is fully offloaded to the GPU) and PR #27293 (`--poll` busy-spin / `--poll 0` recipe) — the default `--poll 50` polling loop accounts for ~1 core, but we observe **2 threads spinning even with no model loaded and no requests**, so this appears to be additional to the poll loop.

Expected:

- An idle llama-server with no models loaded / no requests in flight should block (epoll/futex) and use ~0% CPU.

Happy to run strace/gdb or provide more details.

### Relevant log output

No log output available (issue reproduces with zero requests). Evidence above is from `top -H` and `/proc/<tid>/wchan`.

---

AI usage disclosure: this report was drafted with AI assistance; every claim was verified by direct measurement (`top -H`, `/proc/<tid>/wchan`, resource counters) on the affected deployment before submission.

title: Misc. bug: Misc. bug: --cache-ram -1 is not "no limit": the token cap stays at n_ctx, and with hybrid models RAM grows ~640 MiB per short prompt
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11064, commit a894dae93)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server, Documentation/Github

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-A.gguf --jinja --parallel 1 --kv-unified --ctx-size 196608 --kv-unified-per-slot 196608 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --flash-attn auto --n-gpu-layers 99 --cache-idle-slots --cache-ram -1
workaround in use now: --cache-ram 24576
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Hardware: RTX 5090 32 GB, CUDA 13.4 build, Windows 11, 96 GB RAM. Model: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid `qwen35`, Gated DeltaNet).

What the code does

- `server_prompt_cache(limit_size_mib, limit_tokens)` maps `-1` to `limit_size = 0` (no byte limit); `limit_tokens` is always `n_ctx`.
- `server_prompt_cache::update()`: `limit_tokens_cur = limit_size > 0 ? max(limit_tokens, limit_size/size_per_token) : limit_tokens`. With `-1` the token cap stays at `n_ctx` and never grows; with a positive `--cache-ram` it can.

So `-1`, documented as "no limit", is the only setting where the token cap cannot grow — and it does not bound memory at all.

Why memory still explodes with hybrid/recurrent models

Every saved state carries the recurrent state (~300 MiB here) regardless of prompt length, and every context checkpoint adds about the same again.

Steps to reproduce: start the server with the command line above and send 100 distinct ~1.2k-token prompts one after another, sampling the process private bytes after each. With `--cache-ram -1` each new prompt adds ~640 MiB, linearly (+27.5 GiB after 44 prompts, still growing). With `--cache-ram 24576` the same run plateaus at +23.4 GiB and the log shows `making room for prompt cache entry`.

In production (knowledge-graph extraction: many short prompts) the worker reached 99.7 GiB private bytes on a 96 GiB machine (about 28 GiB of that is the loaded model's own commit on Windows; the cache itself was ~70 GiB). The page file grew to its maximum and Windows raised two "low virtual memory" events. Meanwhile the cache saved only ~4 minutes of prefill over ~36 hours on that workload.

Suggestions

1. Document that `-1` keeps an `n_ctx` token cap and does not bound memory.
2. For recurrent/hybrid models, account for the fixed per-entry state (and checkpoints) in the cap, or warn when `-1` is used with such models.
3. Consider the byte limit as the primary bound; the token cap is a poor proxy when per-entry overhead dominates.


### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. server_prompt_cache::update() and alloc() are the same on master as of 2026-09-23.

### Relevant log output

--cache-ram -1: evictions happen only on the n_ctx token cap; entries are 300-850 MiB each
W srv        update:  - cache token limit (196608, est: 196608) reached, removing oldest entry (size = 845.108 MiB)
W srv        update:  - cache token limit (196608, est: 196608) reached, removing oldest entry (size = 301.047 MiB)

probe: 100 distinct ~1.2k-token prompts, growth of worker private bytes over the loaded-model baseline
--cache-ram -1    : 10 -> +6.2 GiB, 20 -> +12.5, 30 -> +18.7, 40 -> +25.0, stopped at 44 -> +27.5 (linear)
--cache-ram 24576 : 10 -> +6.2 GiB, 20 -> +12.5, 30 -> +18.7, 40..90 -> +23.4 (plateau)
W srv         alloc:  - making room for prompt cache entry, removing oldest entry (size = 637.944 MiB)

title: Vulkan int8-coopmat matmul on RDNA3 (#27952): RX 7900 XTX 27B benchmark data + a small boundary-safety fix
body:
We ran **#27952** ("Vulkan: int8 coopmat quantized matmul for RDNA3/4") through our own Vulkan build on a **Radeon RX 7900 XTX** (gfx1100, 24 GB, PCIe 3.0 x16, no ReBAR, 4-core W-2125) with a **27B** model, and wanted to share the results plus a small related fix.

## Context
On this box the 27B runs on the **Vulkan** backend (~3 GB lighter than ROCm/HIP, more VRAM for context). Model: **Qwen3.8-27B, ROCmFP4-FAST quant (~13.6 GB)**, `MTP n-max 4`, `--flash-attn on`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `-c 131072`.

## A/B benchmark (same GGUF + byte-identical flags, 3 repeats, greedy)

| workload | metric | base Vulkan | +#27952 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent (long-ctx) | prompt t/s | 631.0 | **670.1** | **+6.2%** |
| agent | token t/s | 103.1 | **104.9** | +1.7% |
| agent | MTP draft accept | 88% | **100%** | **+12 pp** |
| agent | wall (s) | 4.89 | **4.70** | -3.9% |
| tools (short-ctx) | prompt t/s | 417.0 | 421.8 | +1.2% |
| tools | token t/s | 117.4 | 117.2 | ~0 |

The gain concentrates on the **prefill-heavy / long-context** workload; the standout is **MTP draft acceptance 88% -> 100%**. Cross-reference: the upstream 7B harness (7900 XTX, ReBAR/PCIe4) reports int8-coopmat at +4.6% dense prefill and +18.5% MoE prefill, decode flat - same shape.

## Small related fix (patch below)

In `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl`, when `K` is not a multiple of `BK*BK_STEP`, the A-operand load reads `ib + ks` past `end_k` - which can land on the next row, or on bytes after the tensor whose f16 scale can be **NaN**. Clamping the block index re-reads the row's first block instead; its B side is zeroed, so it contributes nothing:

```
-                pre_a[li * BK_STEP + ks] = block_a_load(ib + ks, loadr_a);
+                /* K need not be a multiple of BK*BK_STEP: a k-step past end_k re-reads the  */
+                /* row's first block (finite), and its B side is zeroed, so it adds nothing. */
+                /* Reading on past the row instead picks up the next row, or bytes after the */
+                /* tensor whose f16 scale can be NaN.                                         */
+                const uint ib_k = ((blk) + ks * BK < end_k) ? (ib + ks) : ib;
+                pre_a[li * BK_STEP + ks] = block_a_load(ib_k, loadr_a);
```

One-line defensive correctness fix, no measurable cost. (Our `mul_mmq_cm1.comp` is otherwise byte-identical to #27952.)

## Offer
Happy to submit a PR - fold the `mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl` fix into #27952, or as a small follow-up. Can share the benchmark harness if useful.

**Env:** RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) - Mesa 26.2.2 (RADV) - Vulkan - llama.cpp c550d2f6 + #27952.
