body:
### Summary

In the MoE path of `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q` (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cu`), the tail padding of the `src1_q8_1` buffer is computed from `ne11`, which is always **1** for `MUL_MAT_ID` (src1 is `[ne10, 1, n_tokens]`). `ggml_cuda_mmq_get_J_max(type, fallback, cc, 1)` returns **0**, so the buffer gets **no tail padding**, while `mul_mat_q` unconditionally loads a full `J`-column tile of `y` for the last tile of the last used expert. The kernel therefore reads up to `(J-1) * sizeof(block_q8_1_mmq)` bytes past the end of the allocation (≈18 KB for J=128).

Whether this is *observable* depends on how much slack the VMM pool happens to have after that allocation: usually the read lands inside mapped pool memory and nothing happens; for some ubatch sizes the slack is a few KB and the kernel dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

This is still present on master (`fc35562ba4`, "cuda: unblock mmq for MoE on sm_60"), line 206:

```cpp
    const size_t nbytes_src1_q8_1 = ne12*n_expert_used*ne10_padded * y_block_size/y_values_per_block +
        ggml_cuda_mmq_get_J_max(src0->type, fallback, cc, ne11) * sizeof(block_q8_1_mmq);   // ne11 == 1 for mul_mat_id
```

The dense path (line 137) is fine because there `ne11` is the real column count.

### Environment

- RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell (sm_120), CUDA 13, Linux. Build: `GGML_CUDA=ON`, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`.
- MoE model with experts kept on the host (`--cpu-moe`, i.e. `-ot exps=CPU`), so for ubatches ≥ 32 tokens the scheduler copies the used experts to the GPU and runs `MUL_MAT_ID` with MMQ (Q4_K experts, 512 experts, top-10, `ne00=2560`, `ne01=640`).
- Observed on a Qwen4-exp checkpoint (PR #27742 tree), but the buffer math is model-independent; any MoE model that takes the MMQ `mul_mat_id` path with host-resident experts should be affected. Which ubatch sizes crash depends on the pool layout for that model.

### Reproduction (what we measured)

1. Start `llama-server` with the MoE model and `--cpu-moe` (fresh process).
2. Send a prompt whose first ubatch is **508 tokens** (our fork splits a 512-token prompt into `[508, 4]`; on master use `-ub 508` with a longer prompt, or otherwise arrange a 508-token ubatch). Result: `ggml-cuda.cu:107: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` in `MUL_MAT_ID` of the first MoE layer. Same with 1016 tokens. 507, 509, 1021, 2044 etc. are fine.
3. The crash is independent of the prompt *content* (any 512-token slice crashes) and of flash attention.
4. **Pool test**: in a fresh process, first process a 1021-token ubatch, then the 512-token prompt → no crash. The extra earlier allocation grows the VMM pool so the out-of-bounds read stays inside mapped memory. This is what makes the bug look size-specific.
5. Keeping the experts on the CPU for prefill (`GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH=999999`) avoids the path entirely (and, on this box, costs no prefill speed).

Arithmetic for the 508 case (Q4_K, `n_expert_used=10`): `ne_get_rows = 5080`, `src1_q8_1` = 5080·2560·144/128 = 14,630,400 B; pool allocations before it (`ids_src1`, `ids_dst`, `expert_bounds`) put the buffer end 6,784 B below the 2 MiB pool granularity boundary, while the last tile of the highest used expert reads up to 127·144 = 18,288 B past the end. For 507 the slack is 35,584 B and nothing is observed. `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` should report the invalid global read for *both* sizes.

### Fix (one line)

Size the padding from the actual number of `y` columns the kernel can touch (`ne_get_rows`), never from `ne11`:

```diff
--- a/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cu
+++ b/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cu
@@ -203,7 +203,7 @@ void ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q(
     const size_t nbytes_src1_q8_1 = ne12*n_expert_used*ne10_padded * y_block_size/y_values_per_block +
-        ggml_cuda_mmq_get_J_max(src0->type, fallback, cc, ne11) * sizeof(block_q8_1_mmq);
+        ggml_cuda_mmq_get_J_max(src0->type, fallback, cc, std::max<int64_t>(ne_get_rows, 128)) * sizeof(block_q8_1_mmq);
```

With this patch the 508/1016-token cases pass and the outputs of the previously working sizes are unchanged (the padding is never read into results). Happy to open a PR if you prefer.

title: Misc. bug: Openvino cannot run gemma on intel core 7 155h
body:
### Name and Version

version [b11113](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11113)



### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -hf unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I don't  think this will fixed at least not satisfactorily. The NPU in the intel core 7 ultra 155h only supports up to 255 models per process which surpasses the over 700 required for gemma, so weights have to be compiled on the fly for the NPU, which is very slow. 

This was heavlily AI assisted: this is my first time touching hardware. i used deepseek v4.1 and the oh my pi harness. i wondered why no one ever talked about using the npu for running ai on laptops, it's because the npu does not support enough models for gemma, or the supported models are too old and not SOTA. 

technically openvino does have a huggingface repo https://huggingface.co/collections/OpenVINO/llms-optimized-for-npu and documentation https://docs.openvino.ai/2025/openvino-workflow-generative/inference-with-genai/inference-with-genai-on-npu.html on how to run LLMs but that's not really the idea of llama.cpp and they require a lot of setup. and the models on huggingface are outdated maybe this is why?. i am using vulkan now on the GPU instead of the NPU for now. i might try using the openvino documentatoin on running llms next 

i am posting this so that no one else wastes 3 days going this route. 

After **255 successful `zeCommandQueueCreate` calls in one context**, the next one fails with

```
L0 zeCommandQueueCreate result: ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED, code 0x78000001 - driver is not initialized
```

while the device and driver are perfectly healthy. The kernel logs the real reason at the same time:

```
intel_vpu 0000:00:0b.0: [drm] *ERROR* ivpu_cmdq_create(): Failed to allocate command queue ID: -16
```

`-16` is `-EBUSY` from the command queue ID allocation (`IVPU_CMDQ_MIN_ID 1` .. `IVPU_CMDQ_MAX_ID 255`,
`drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_drv.h`), i.e. the per-context pool of 255 command queue IDs is full. The
reported `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED` / "driver is not initialized" is misleading: nothing is
uninitialised, the queue budget is exhausted.

This is easy to hit with LLM workloads: the OpenVINO NPU plugin creates **one command queue per
compiled model** (`ZeroCommandQueue::create` from `Plugin::compile_model`,
`src/plugins/intel_npu/src/plugin/src/plugin.cpp`), and pipelines that compile per-layer or
per-subgraph models hold hundreds of them at once. Concretely, llama.cpp's OpenVINO backend
compiles one OpenVINO model per graph fragment and keeps them alive, so a gemma-3-1b run reaches
~419 compilations for the prefill graph alone and dies on the 256th, after which the backend logs
`device NPU is not available, fallback to CPU` and silently runs on the CPU.

## Environment

- Intel Core Ultra 7 155H (Meteor Lake), NPU37XX, PCI `0000:00:0b.0`
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel `7.0.0-31-generic`, `intel_vpu` 1.0.0 (`Scheduler mode: HW`)
- NPU firmware: `vpu_37xx_v1.bin` 20260630 (`MTL_CLIENT_SILICON-NVR+NN-deployment`) - also seen with
  20260219; the failure is identical with both
- UMD: `intel-level-zero-npu` 1.38.0 (from the `linux-npu-driver` v1.38.0 Ubuntu 24.04 tarball,
  used via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`) - and the same with 1.35.0 (snap)
- Level Zero loader: `libze_loader.so.1.28.2` (Ubuntu `libze-dev`)
- OpenVINO: 2026.4.0 (python wheel and runtime archive; both NPU plugins reproduce)

## Minimal reproduction (no llama.cpp needed)

```python
import numpy as np
import openvino as ov

core = ov.Core()
p = ov.opset13.parameter([1, 4], ov.Type.f32, name="x")
model = ov.Model([ov.opset13.relu(p)], [p], "relu_test")
cfg = {"NPU_USE_NPUW": "YES", "NPUW_DEVICES": "NPU", "NPUW_WEIGHTS_BANK": "shared"}

kept = []                                  # hold them alive: one queue each
for i in range(300):
    kept.append(core.compile_model(model, "NPU", cfg))
```

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<umd-1.38.0>:<openvino-runtime> python npu_hold_test.py
compile 255 FAILED while holding 255 compiled models:
  L0 zeCommandQueueCreate result: ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED, code 0x78000001 - driver is not initialized
```

Failure at exactly 255, every time. Controls, same driver/loader/device:

- one `compile_model` + one `infer` on the NPU: **OK** (`relu([-1,2,-3,4]) == [0,2,0,4]`)
- 300 `compile_model` calls **without** holding them alive (each released before the next): **OK**
- 64 infer requests created from one compiled model: **OK**

So the limit is the number of *simultaneously live* compiled models in one process.

## Reproduction with llama.cpp (the real-world case)

```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<umd-1.38.0>:<openvino-runtime> \
ZE_ENABLE_ALT_DRIVERS=libze_intel_npu.so.1 \
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=NPU \
GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_COMPILE_CONFIG='enable-shave-ddr-access-optimization=true' \
llama-cli -m gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf -c 256 -n 8 -p 'The capital of France is' -st --no-mmproj
```

```
Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:117:          (Core::compile_model)
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:54:
Exception from src/plugins/intel_npu/src/plugin/src/plugin.cpp:578:   (CompiledModel ctor)
Exception from src/plugins/intel_npu/src/utils/src/zero/zero_wrappers.cpp:321:  (ZeroCommandQueue::create)
L0 zeCommandQueueCreate result: ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED, code 0x78000001 - driver is not initialized
```

Number of OpenVINO models compiled for `gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M` in that setup (counted by
instrumenting the translation entry, same numbers on the CPU device so no NPU needed):

| `-n` (decode steps) | compilations |
|---------------------|--------------|
| 1                   | 499          |
| 3                   | 659          |
| 4                   | 738          |

i.e. ~419 for the prefill graph alone (about 210 scheduler fragments x 2 phases), ~80 more per
decode step. All of them are live at once, so the 256th fails during the first prefill.

## Expected

- A queue-budget exhaustion should not be reported as `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED` /
  "driver is not initialized". `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` (or
  `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`) plus a message naming the limit would let consumers react
  (retry later, release compiled models, fall back to another device) instead of debugging a
  phantom initialisation failure.
- Please confirm whether 255 command queues per context is the intended budget for the HW-scheduler
  path (`Scheduler mode: HW`) on NPU37XX, and whether it can be raised or made dynamic. If it is a
  hard limit, it needs documenting: with one queue per compiled model it caps the number of
  concurrently live compiled models, which is a normal pattern for LLM pipelines.
- The `ivpu_cmdq_create()` line is logged as `*ERROR*` but the failure is a resource limit, not a
  driver error; it would help to log the current/max queue count with it.

## Notes / caveats

- Not a wedged device: the queue IDs belong to the context and are released when the process exits.
  A trivial compile works again immediately after a failing run. Reports of an NPU that "needs a
  reboot" after such a failure are this same per-process exhaustion: the failing process is the one
  that needs more queues than exist.
- A module reload (`modprobe -r intel_vpu && modprobe intel_vpu`) and a PCI function-level reset
  (`echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:00:0b.0/reset`, then unbind/bind) both re-initialise the
  device cleanly; neither changes the outcome, which is consistent with a per-context budget.
- The 255 model compilations in the python reproducer are tiny (`Relu` on `[1,4]`) and take under a
  second in total, so the limit is reached long before any memory or time pressure.
- Cross-reference for the OpenVINO side: creating one command queue per compiled model makes any
  pipeline that keeps many compiled models alive fail here; a shared/pooled command queue per
  context, or releasing the queue when the model is released, would avoid the cliff.

title: Eval bug: Bailing V3 (Ling 3.0) autoparser lacks a <tool_call> reasoning terminator but emits these often mid-reasoning
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10540, commit 07822bddf)
built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395)

### Models

Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M from https://huggingface.co/bloomer010/Ling-3.0-flash-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

In a multi-turn tool using chat, the model sometimes emits `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` from inside its reasoning channel and stops without ever closing `</think>`. The whole turn is then swallowed into reasoning_content.

Root cause
Bailing V3 has no specialized parser in common/chat.cpp, so it falls through to the generic autoparser, which sets a single reasoning terminator (`thinking_end_tags = {"</think>"}`) with no <tool_call> fallback. When the model opens a tool call before closing `</think>`, nothing terminates reasoning and the output is mis-routed.

Behaviour like this is already handled for some other models (these thinking+tool models add tool call openers as reasoning terminators).

For example:
Qwen3-Coder: `thinking_end_tags = {"</think>", "<tool_call>"}`
DeepSeek V3.2: `thinking_end_tags = {THINK_END, FC_START}`
Kimi K2 (common_chat_params_init_kimi_k2) handles this exact behavior, with the maintainer comment: "this model is CRAZY … it can call tools at the end of reasoning without closing reasoning", and adds `<|tool_calls_section_begin|> / <|tool_call_begin|>` as terminators.
Bailing V3's Kimi-K2-like tendency to call tools mid-reasoning isn't covered by the generic autoparser.

Suggested fix
Add <tool_call> to Bailing V3's reasoning terminators (similar to Kimi K2/Qwen3-Coder fixes)

Reproduction code I used to test this exact behaviour which produces a high fail rate with Ling 3.0 flash:
https://gist.github.com/chielteuben/54efbb6b1a75eb7310246f34c54e3465

_No response_

Easily reproduceable using the gist I added.

title: Feature Request: Fast Tool Gating & Single-Pass Selection via Prefill Logit Slicing
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

## Motivation
In modern agentic workflows (e.g., ReAct, function calling, tool use), models spend significant wall-clock time autoregressively generating tokens just to make discrete routing decisions (e.g., spelling out `<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_weather"...}`).

## What is the proposed solution
A special agent mode to fasten tool calls through "Jev-like" hybrid mode

Currently, when tools are provided in `llama-server` or `llama-cli`:
1. The engine prefills the prompt.
2. It enters the autoregressive decode loop ($O(N)$ sequential token passes) using either GBNF grammar constraints or hoping the chat template emits tool tokens correctly.
3. If the model chooses *not* to call a tool, or chooses a simple tool, we still pay the latency penalty of sequential token decoding and grammar state-machine transitions before knowing the routing outcome.

Because the prompt prefill pass **already computes the full KV cache and logits for the final prompt token**, we can resolve binary tool-gating decisions and tool-name enums in **$O(1)$ single forward passes** via logit slicing, falling back seamlessly to standard text generation without wasting the prefilled KV cache.

---

## Proposed Architectural Flow

```
[Prompt + Registered Tools] 
          │
          ▼
   llama_decode() (Prefill)
          │
          ▼
Inspect logits of last token: P(Tool Call) vs P(Chat/Text)
          │
   ┌──────┴────────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                       ▼
P(Chat) > Threshold               P(Tool) > Threshold
   │                                       │
   │ (Zero KV cache waste)                 ▼
   │ Direct stream to user        Slice logits over registered 
   │ (Standard Autoregressive)    tool names: P(tool_1...tool_N)
                                           │
                                  ┌────────┴─────────────────┐
                                  ▼                          ▼
                         Bounded Enums/Booleans     Unbounded String Args
                         (Parallel Logit Slices)    (Switch to GBNF / AR loop)
```

### 1. Zero-Cost Gating Check (Prefill Inspection)
Right after `llama_decode()` on the prompt batch, before initializing the autoregressive decode loop:
* Inspect the logits of the final sequence position (`llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1)`).
* Measure the probability mass of the model's tool delimiter token (e.g., `<tool_call>`, `[TOOL]`, or `{` depending on the active Jinja chat template) against normal text tokens.
* **If text generation is chosen:** Continue the decode loop immediately. The KV cache is already fully initialized; overhead is virtually $0$ ms.

### 2. $O(1)$ Discrete Tool Selection
If the model indicates a tool call:
* Instead of sequentially generating the tool name string (e.g., `"name": "get_weather_data"` across multiple decode steps), the engine can mask the logits over the first tokens of the user-registered tools:
  $$\text{Softmax}\left(\text{logits}[\text{id}(\text{tool}_1), \text{id}(\text{tool}_2), \dots]\right)$$
* Select the candidate with highest calibrated confidence in a single step.

### 3. Argument Resolution Split
* **Bounded arguments (Enums, Booleans):** Handled via single-pass logit slicing.
* **Unbounded arguments (Raw strings, free text):** Switch back to standard autoregressive generation, with GBNF constrained only to that specific string argument.

---

## Key Benefits
1. **Dramatic Latency Reduction in Agent Loops:** Eliminates 10–50 sequential autoregressive steps for routing decisions, reducing decision latency to the prefill time (~15–40 ms on modern hardware).
2. **Zero Wasted Computation on Fallback:** Because the prompt prefill already took place, falling back to standard conversational text streaming incurs zero recomputation or KV-cache invalidation.
3. **No Syntax Failures for Tool Routing:** Eliminates malformed tool name keys and invalid enum tool selections at the root.

---



## Alternatives Considered
* **Full GBNF Grammar Decoding:** Guarantees syntax correctness, but incurs full sequential decode latency ($O(N)$ forward passes) even for basic if/else decisions.
* **Draft Model Speculative Decoding:** Requires loading a second model into VRAM and doesn't solve the structural inefficiency of using autoregression for discrete enum selection.


### Motivation

Save a lot of inference and compute when performing tool calls

### Possible Implementation


1. **`llama-server` (`/v1/chat/completions`):**
   * Introduce an optional flag, e.g., `--speculative-tool-gating` or a request parameter `"tool_choice": "auto_fast"`.
   * If enabled, check the top-K logits of the prefill output against the model's configured tool-call trigger tokens before attaching the full GBNF grammar parser.
2. **C API (`llama.h`):**
   * Expose a helper utility or sampler stage:
     ```c
     // Evaluates probabilities exclusively across a masked subset of candidate tokens
     // on the current prefilled context position without advancing the decode sequence.
     LLAMA_API void llama_sample_token_distribution(
         struct llama_context * ctx,
         const llama_token    * candidate_tokens,
         size_t                 n_candidates,
         float                * out_probs
     );
     ```

### Edge Case: Multi-Token Tool Names & Shared Prefixes

To handle tools that share initial tokens (e.g., `get_weather` vs `get_stock`):

1. **Trie-Based Logit Slicing:** Construct a Token Trie of registered tools. Non-branching prefixes are auto-advanced, and logit slicing only triggers at branching nodes (reducing steps from full JSON generation to Trie depth $D \le 2$).
2. **Batched Sequence Evaluation:** Alternatively, fork the existing context KV-cache across candidate tool sequences in a single batched `llama_decode()` pass to score cumulative log-probabilities in $O(1)$ time. (seems MTP/DFlash friendly to me)
3. **Index Token Aliasing:** In `llama-server`, map tools to discrete index tokens `[A, B, C]` within the tool definition template to ensure candidate IDs are always strictly 1 token.

title: Feature Request: SYCL per-instance queue, device-side events,  async copy
Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets
body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.



### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

```
ankk98@ankk98-workstation:~/repos/llama.cpp$ fastfetch
             .',;::::;,'.                 ankk98@ankk98-workstation
         .';:cccccccccccc:;,.             -------------------------
      .;cccccccccccccccccccccc;.          OS: Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation Edition) x86_64
    .:cccccccccccccccccccccccccc:.        Host: ROG Flow Z13 GZ302EA_GZ302EA (1.0)
  .;ccccccccccccc;.:dddl:.;ccccccc;.      Kernel: Linux 7.1.3-200.fc44.x86_64
 .:ccccccccccccc;OWMKOOXMWd;ccccccc:.     Uptime: 4 hours, 48 mins
.:ccccccccccccc;KMMc;cc;xMMc;ccccccc:.    Packages: 4 (appimage), 31 (flatpak), 3569 (rpm)
```

title: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid Gated DeltaNet): decode throughput collapses ~25x at context positions >~80K while prompt processing stays fast
body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).

title: Eval bug: llama-server aborts on GGML_ASSERT(batch.slot_batched || batch.size() == 0) after "got exception: bad allocation" in a slot (b11159, Gemma 4 31B, prefix reuse)
body:
### Name and Version

```
llama-server version: b11159 (6b790a9c2), Windows x64, CUDA 13.4 build (llama-b11159-bin-win-cuda-13.4-x64.zip)
```

Not reproduced on b10679 (50f068fff, cuda-13.3 build) under the same workload — see below.

### Operating systems

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

RTX 3090 24 GB (driver 616.92, CUDA 13.4), 32 GB RAM

### Models

gemma-4-31B-it-QAT-Q4_0.gguf (lmstudio-community/gemma-4-31B-it-QAT-GGUF)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

llama-server aborts the whole process after an exception inside one slot, instead of failing that request.

In a multi-turn chat workload (a test harness replaying a 15-turn conversation with tool calls, prompts ~4-7k tokens, one slot), a request that the server routed by prefix reuse failed with `got exception: bad allocation`, and the server then hit:

```
tools/server/server-context.cpp:2846: GGML_ASSERT(batch.slot_batched || batch.size() == 0) failed
```

and exited. Every later request got a connection error.

Launch flags:

```
llama-server -m gemma-4-31B-it-QAT-Q4_0.gguf -cram 0 -c 32768 -ngl 99 -fa on --load-mode none -np 1 -t 8 -b 2048 -ub 512 --chat-template-file <gemma4 template> --port 1234
```

Host RAM was at 56% with the pagefile unused when it happened, so this was not the machine running out of memory. VRAM was near full (~400 MB free).

**Why the process aborts rather than failing one request.** In the prompt-processing callback of `update_slots()`, a slot adds its prompt tokens to the shared batch (`batch.add(slot.id, cur_tok, ...)`, ~line 3542 in b11159), then may call `create_checkpoint(slot, ...)` (~line 3634), and only at the end of the lambda sets `slot_batched = &slot` (~line 3639). If anything between the first `batch.add` and that assignment throws, `iterate()` catches it, logs `got exception`, sends the error and calls `slot.release()` — but the tokens already added to the batch stay there and `slot_batched` is still `nullptr`. The next statement after `pre_decode()` is `GGML_ASSERT(batch.slot_batched || batch.size() == 0)`, which then fails. The same `iterate()` handler and the same assert exist in b10679, so the abort path itself is not new; what is new in our case is that something in that window started throwing. `create_checkpoint` (which serializes sequence state into host memory) is the allocation in that window, which makes it the likely source of the `bad_alloc`, but the log does not show which call threw — checkpoint creation is only logged at trace level.

Two changes that might be relevant:

1. Abort-vs-fail: when a slot's callback throws after adding tokens, the batch should be cleared (or the slot's tokens removed) before the assert, so one failed request does not take the server down.
2. The throw itself: the checkpoint-handling diff between b10679 and b11159 in `server-context.cpp` (checkpoints pruned only once the list is full; a checkpoint at the same `n_tokens` now superseding the old one) is the change in that area between the two builds.

Related but, as far as I can tell, different: #27451 (hardens `bad_alloc` in prompt-*cache* insertion — we run with `-cram 0`) and #27530 (cleanup after failed state restores).

**Comparison.** Same harness, same flags, same model, same VRAM headroom (373 MB vs 404 MB free), run back to back:

| build | requests served | prefix-reuse requests | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| b11159 (cuda-13.4) | 33 | 11 | `bad allocation` → assert → process exit |
| b10679 (cuda-13.3) | 174 | 28 | full run completed, no errors |

Not reduced to a minimal repro yet — it has only happened once, after 11 prefix-reuse requests, so a single short test may not trigger it.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown — between b10679 (50f068fff), where the same workload ran clean, and b11159 (6b790a9c2).

### Relevant log output

```
13.48.164.669 I slot print_timing: id  0 | task 22990 |    graphs reused =      22926
13.48.165.116 I slot      release: id  0 | task 22990 | stop processing: n_tokens = 6878, truncated = 0
13.48.235.454 I slot get_availabl: id  0 | task -1 | selected slot by LCP similarity, f_sim_best = 0.981 (> 0.100 thold), f_keep = 0.991

D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/tools/server/server-context.cpp:2846: GGML_ASSERT(batch.slot_batched || batch.size() == 0) failed
```

title: Misc. bug: server dies under sustained image traffic — ubatch assert at small -ub, silent SIGKILL at large -ub (Gemma 12B QAT + mmproj)
body:
Hi, first of all thank you for llama.cpp — it runs my daily driver bot and
it's great. I'm fairly new to debugging this deep, so please let me know if
I'm holding it wrong or if there's a diagnostic you'd like me to run. Happy
to bisect or test anything.

## Name and Version

```
$ llama --version
version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11046, commit 60081bb2b)
built with Clang 19.1.7 for Linux x86_64
```

## Operating systems

Linux (CachyOS / Arch family, x86_64, RTX 3060 12GB, CUDA)

## Which modules are affected

llama-server, libllama (core library)

## Command line

```
llama serve -m /mnt/D/Mymodels/gemma412b/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --mmproj /mnt/D/Mymodels/gemma412b/mmproj-BF16.gguf \
  --model-draft /mnt/D/Mymodels/gemma412b/mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 \
  --fit off -ngl 99 -fa on -c 16384 --load-mode none --jinja -np 1 \
  -ub 8192 -b 1024 --image-min-tokens 1024
```

Model files: Gemma 12B IT QAT (`UD-Q4_K_XL`), matching `mmproj-BF16.gguf`,
and a community MTP draft (`mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf`).

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

The server serves text perfectly (1000+ token generations, ~70-80 tok/s
with the MTP draft, never a hiccup), but **dies when serving images
repeatedly**. It takes a while — roughly 5+ images exchanged one by one in a
chat session — and then the process is gone with no error line in the log.
My shell just reports:

```
fish: Job 1, 'llama serve -m /mnt/D/Mymodels/…' terminated by signal SIGKILL (Forced quit)
```

There are two flavors of this I've seen, possibly related:

**Flavor A (loud, understood):** with a small `-ub` (default 512), the first
large image kills the server immediately with:

```
llamacpp/src/llama-context.cpp: GGML_ASSERT((cparams.causal_attn ||
cparams.n_ubatch >= n_tokens_all) && "non-causal attention requires
n_ubatch >= n_tokens") failed
```

That one makes sense to me — image embeddings need non-causal attention and
don't fit the micro-batch. Raising `-ub` fixes it deterministically.

**Flavor B (silent, the actual report):** with `-ub` raised (2024, then
8192), the assert is gone and dozens of image tasks complete fine —
including 2000+ token ones — but after sustained image traffic the process
still dies with SIGKILL and *nothing* in the log. 8GB+ free on both VRAM and
system RAM at the time, so it's not OOM as far as I can tell. Bigger `-ub`
delays the death but doesn't prevent it, which makes me think something
accumulates per image (context keeps the image tokens; my client re-sends
history) until some ceiling is hit on a path that doesn't print.

Repro sketch: serve the above command, send images one by one through
`/v1/chat/completions` (screenshots, ~1000 tokens of image content each,
history retained so context grows), wait. For me it dies after a handful of
images at `-ub 2024` and noticeably later at `-ub 8192`.

## What I already tried (and failed)

- Raising `-ub` 512 → 2024 → 8192 (and now testing 16384): fixes flavor A
  completely, only *delays* flavor B.
- `--image-min-tokens 1024` / default: crash happens either way once enough
  images accumulate (kept at 1024 for small-image detail).
- Disabling the MTP draft was my first suspect, but the assert deaths
  reproduce with **zero speculative flags** on plain commands, so spec
  decoding can't be the required cause. Text + spec decoding is flawless.
- Checked VRAM (`nvidia-smi`) and RAM (`free -h`) at max context: 8GB+ free
  on both. Not resource exhaustion as far as I can see.
- Text-only sessions of any length: never crash. It is image traffic
  specifically.

Possibly related issues I found (couldn't quite match mine, but close):
#22867 (MTP + vision slot corruption), #21550 (Gemma crashes when
image-min-tokens raised), #24366 (Gemma MTP buffer issue), #21461 (the
ubatch assert history).

## First Bad Commit

Unknown — I only run recent builds (11046). The ubatch assert threads above
go back a while, but the silent flavor I can only vouch for on this build.

## Excerpt from my run (`-ub 8192 --image-min-tokens 1024`)

title: Feature Request: avoid allocating logits buffer for encoder-only models
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

It is my understanding that `llama_context::output_reserve()` still fully allocates logits buffer for encoder-only models (BERT / XLM-RoBERTa: bge-m3, nomic-embed), which should never use those for their purpose. Local tests showing RAM memory growth compatible with `n_tokens` which leads me to believe it allocates the expected logits buffer by current logic (fix/design for #14204) 

```bash
=== bge-m3-f16.gguf
{"n_tokens":2000,"dim":1024}
n_vocab=250002  RSS before=796MiB after=2869MiB  growth=2074MiB
expected logits buffer n_vocab*N*4 = 1907MiB
=== nomic-embed-text-v1.5.f16.gguf
{"n_tokens":2000,"dim":768}
n_vocab=30522  RSS before=296MiB after=713MiB  growth=417MiB
expected logits buffer n_vocab*N*4 = 233MiB
```

My main hypothesis is that we really don't need that buffer in encoder-only models, so it would be nice to keep it free if that confirms.  

### Motivation

That memory is expensive (`(n_vocab * n_tokens * 4)` bytes) and from what I can see is RAM only, which makes it hard for smaller setups (homelab, consumer hardware).

### Possible Implementation

[#25964](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25964) would be relevant here as an opt-in `--no-logits-for-embeddings` flag potentially would apply here. However I think there's a simpler fix by just checking if the model has logits in the first place:
- At init: llama_context[ already builds a reserve graph](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-context.cpp#L676-L688) for prompt processing (`graph_reserve()`, then `get_gf_res_reserve()`. Right after that, record whether that graph has a logits output: `get_gf_res_reserve()->get_logits() != nullptr`.
- In [output_reserve():](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/src/llama-context.cpp#L676-L688) use that recorded flag instead of has_logits = true. Keep the T5 special case as it is.

title: Feature Request: CPU Flash Attention does not use the selected KleidiAI SME2 kernel
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).

- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

In the baseline commit: a894dae939d426954ce54bb604824f1ae918a0c5, QK and AV call simd_gemm() at ops.cpp:9037 and ops.cpp:9100.

It is expected that the eligible tiles use the selected SME2 F32 kernel whereas in unsupported cases retain fallback to SIMD.

### Motivation

SME2 hardware is available but unused by CPU Flash Attention. Main expected benefit is Arm prompt-processing performance accelerated with SME2 microkernels in KleidiAI. 

Attention semantics and -fa auto policy remain unchanged.

### Possible Implementation

- Query opaque KleidiAI workspace.
- Pack Q once per query tile.
- Bind K/V packing to the selected descriptor.
- Use SME2 for QK and AV.
- Preserve simd_gemm() fallback

title: CUDA: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default (silent CPU fallback for 4-bit KV)
body:
Building with the default flags, using a 4-bit KV cache (q4_0/q4_1) silently drops prefill to CPU speed. No warning, no offload message, just a ~30x slowdown that is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

What happens: the kernel selection in fattn.cu (ggml_cuda_fattn_kv_type_supported) only accepts f16/f32 KV unless GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS is set at compile time. When the requested KV type is not supported, the scheduler places the whole FLASH_ATTN_EXT op on the CPU backend.

Measured on a single RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B, K=q4_1 / V=q8_0, 130K ctx:

| build | prefill |
|---|---|
| default | ~34 t/s |
| -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON | 659-1094 t/s depending on context |

This is the third report of the same silent fallback in #27109 (myself, @aand18, @Cybertiron). Every user who wants 4-bit KV to fit long contexts in limited VRAM has to discover this flag on their own, and release builds ship without it.

Ask: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default in the CMake option, or at minimum print a clear warning at startup when the requested KV cache types cannot be served by the CUDA FA kernel.

PR #28634 flips the default.

title: Misc. bug: /slots save/restore never persists the draft-model context (ctx_dft) on speculative-decoding deployments
body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit 0f3a71b)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Reproduced against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` commit `0f3a71be15af836d277c9f918adfafb45732677e`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -fa on \
  --slot-save-path /slot-cache
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore` only persists `ctx_tgt` (via
`llama_state_seq_save_file`/`llama_state_seq_load_file`) — on a deployment
running speculative decoding (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`), the draft
model's own context (`ctx_dft`) is never captured or restored at all.

This is a separate, narrower gap from #25913 (checkpoints not persisted,
addressed by #26004): even once #26004 lands, a restored slot's draft
model only gets its state back if a checkpoint happened to already exist
at save time (checkpoints carry their own `data_dft`) — a short
conversation that hasn't hit its first checkpoint yet restores with an
empty draft-model KV cache and no fallback. The raw, currently-live
`ctx_dft` state is simply discarded on save, independent of checkpoint
existence.

Not directly observable as a crash or an error — the restore reports
success either way — but on a speculative-decoding deployment it means
the draft model silently starts cold after every restore whenever no
checkpoint happens to cover the request, undermining part of the benefit
`--slot-save-path` is meant to provide alongside #26004's fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server` with a draft model (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`)
   and `--slot-save-path`.
2. Send a short prompt (short enough that it completes before the first
   context checkpoint would be created) with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`.
4. Inspect the save file: only the `ctx_tgt` payload
   (`llama_state_seq_save_file`'s own format) is present; there is no
   companion draft-model state anywhere.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
6. The restore succeeds and reports the correct token count, but
   `ctx_dft` was never touched — the draft model's KV cache is empty,
   identical to a slot that just came up cold, regardless of what #26004
   restores for `ctx_tgt`/checkpoints.

### First bad commit

Not a regression — `SLOT_SAVE`/`SLOT_RESTORE` have never captured
`ctx_dft`; this predates both this report and #26004.

### Relationship to other issues/PRs

- #25913 / #26004: separate root cause (missing checkpoint persistence
  for `ctx_tgt`'s reuse-validity check), already well covered there. This
  report is about `ctx_dft` specifically, which #26004 does not touch.
- We have a working fix (raw `ctx_dft` capture/restore via
  `llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`/`get_data_ext`/`set_data_ext`, stored as
  a companion `<save-file>.dft`, verified live on a production
  Vulkan/AMD-APU draft-mtp deployment) and are happy to open it as a PR,
  either standalone or as a follow-up once #26004 merges (to avoid
  competing for review attention on the same file/handlers at once) —
  see our comment on #26004 for details.

title: ggml_gallocr silently reuses stale allocation plan on identity change at fixed position (sparse MoE corruption)
body:
### Summary

`ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` reuses a stale allocation plan when a node at the **same graph position** changes **identity** but not size — silent memory corruption on repeated `ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph()` calls with dynamic-topology graphs (sparse MoE routing).

### File / functions

`ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c` — `ggml_gallocr_node_needs_realloc` (~line 997), `ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc` (~line 1009), `ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph` (~line 1052).

### Root cause

```c
static bool ggml_gallocr_node_needs_realloc(ggml_gallocr_t galloc, struct ggml_tensor * node, struct tensor_alloc * talloc) {
    size_t node_size = 0;
    if (!node->data && !node->view_src) {
        if (talloc->buffer_id < 0) {
            return false;
        }
        node_size = ggml_backend_buft_get_alloc_size(galloc->bufts[talloc->buffer_id], node);
    }
    return talloc->size_max >= node_size;   // <-- SIZE ONLY, no identity/op/shape comparison
}
```

`ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` calls this once per node and once per non-NULL `src[j]`, indexed purely by **position** `i` in `graph->nodes[]` — it never checks that `graph->nodes[i]` is the same logical tensor as when the plan for that position was built, only that node/leaf counts and per-position byte size still fit.

If a backend's scheduler (or any dynamic-topology graph builder — sparse MoE routing is the clearest trigger) produces two graphs where position `i` holds two *different* tensors that happen to have a compatible size, `ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` returns `false`, the stale offset table is silently reused, and the new tensor is written into memory reserved for the old one — **no error, no assertion, no warning** at any log level.

This is distinct from the already-fixed ggml-org/ggml#999 ("gallocr: fix reallocation of shared tensors", closed 2024-10-31), which addressed conflicting allocations for tensors *shared between graphs*. This is about a single graph position silently changing identity between successive calls on the *same* `ggml_gallocr_t` — a different code path, still present.

### Reproduction (real hardware, two independent cases)

Qualcomm Hexagon NPU backend (`ggml-hexagon`), OnePlus 15 / Snapdragon SM8850, batch-1 decode of sparse-MoE models. A local diagnostic patch (not upstream — hashes node op+name+shape into a signature and compares it in addition to the stock size-only check) demonstrates exactly which invariant fails:

**1. `gemma-4-26B-A4B.Q2_K.gguf`** (Gemma4 MoE), reproduced both HTP-offloaded **and CPU-only** (`-ngl 0`), ruling out anything NPU-specific:

```
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 2639 (result_norm):
plan signature 618212584c166e89, current de842b29e5861e97
(counts/sizes matched, but tensor at this position differs from the one the plan was built for
— possible silent corruption if plan is reused)
```

**2. `Marco-Nano-Instruct.Q4_0.gguf`** (Qwen3-MoE, 256 experts/8 active), separate build/commit:

```
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 1876 (ffn_moe_weighted-27 (view)): ...
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 1892 (result_norm): ...
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 1893 (result_output): ...
```

Same pattern on a different model/build — general MoE / dynamic-topology issue in the allocator's reuse check, not model- or build-specific.

Observed symptom in both cases at the application level: **silently corrupted output** (grammatically-shaped but semantically incoherent text / garbage tokens), no crash, no error at default log level.

### Suggested fix

Compare a cheap identity signature (e.g. `node->op`, `node->name`/interned id, shape) in addition to size in `ggml_gallocr_node_needs_realloc()`. If it differs from what was recorded when the plan for that position was built, force a realloc for that node (ideally just that node, to avoid regressing the fast-path the plan cache exists for).

### Why this likely hasn't surfaced widely

Requires (a) reusing the same `ggml_gallocr_t` across many calls — standard for decode loops — and (b) runtime-dependent graph topology at fixed node/leaf count, which is rare outside sparse-MoE routing or custom schedulers that reorder nodes non-canonically between calls. Dense models essentially never trigger it since their graph shape is static token-to-token.

### Environment

- Device: OnePlus 15 (Snapdragon SM8850), Android
- Backend: `ggml-hexagon` fork (HTP0), reproduced both HTP-offload and CPU-only
- Models: `gemma-4-26B-A4B.Q2_K.gguf` (Gemma4 MoE), `Marco-Nano-Instruct.Q4_0.gguf` (Qwen3-MoE)

🤖 Report compiled with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Eval bug: qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) on Metal: decode emits 1 token then EOS at long context — silent empty output, stochastic at threshold, threshold moves with model quant / KV quant / n_ctx
body:
### Name and Version
0.3.0-dev (build 37, commit 8e53fce), built with AppleClang 21.0.0 for Darwin arm64 (Metal, default flags, Release)

### Operating systems
Mac

### GGML backends
Metal

### Hardware
2x Apple M1 Max (24-core and 32-core GPU), 64 GB unified memory each — reproduced on both

### Models
- unsloth-style AD-3.84bpw-IQ4_XS-M64 (28 shards) — 16K/64K OK, 128K FAIL
- AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64 (33 shards) — 64K FAIL (q4v4 KV) / 16K FAIL (q8v8 KV)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce
llama-server, single slot, GPU flash attention (auto). With prompts beyond a config-dependent threshold:
- prefill completes normally (e.g. 118-140 tok/s at 64K)
- decode emits exactly 1 token then stops (EOS): `eval time = ... / 1 tokens`, answer empty
- server returns HTTP 200 — silent failure, no error anywhere
- at/near the threshold the failure is STOCHASTIC: same server, same config, same prompt size → 64K x3 = PASS, PASS, FAIL on consecutive runs
- threshold moves with model quant (Q4_K_M << IQ4_XS), KV quant (q8v8+b256: 16K vs q4v4+b512: 64K), and possibly n_ctx window size (64K probes 3/3 @ n_ctx 208896 vs 2/3 @ n_ctx 262144, same 64K prompts)
- with mixed-precision KV (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q4_0) Metal rejects FA → attention falls back to CPU → 200K needle tests pass 3/3 (correct but slow) — so the failure is specific to the GPU attention path
- `-fa off` cannot be tested with quantized KV ("quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled"); with f16 KV + `-fa off` decode fails immediately with `Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 256, ret = -3` on the first token
- memory pressure excluded (failures observed with < 600 MB swap)
- needle-in-haystack probe (3 pins at 10/50/90% depth), warmup, temperature 0

Matrix (all llama-server, GPU FA, IQ4_XS unless noted):
| model | KV | -b/-ub | n_ctx | 16K | 64K | 128K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | 3/3 | 3/3,3/3,3/3 | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 1024 | 208896 (A machine, +ngram spec) | — | 3/3 (32K/64K) | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q8v8 | 1024 | 262144 | — | 3/3,3/3,0/3 (stochastic!) | not reached |
| Q4_K_M | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | — | 0/3 | — |
| Q4_K_M | q8v8 | 256 | 208896 | 0/3 | — | — |

### First Bad Commit
Unknown; qwen4exp support landed via #27742 (2026-08-27) — all failures observed on builds containing it. **Retested on master `df03399` (0.4.0-dev build 300, contains #27941, #28023, #28098): the bug reproduces identically.** 64K x1 = 3/3 (prefill 153.8 tok/s, decode 11.1 — sparse-FA perf improvements visible), 128K x1 = **0/3, decode 0.0 (1 tok)** — same signature, same threshold. So #27941 (block position keying), #28023 (indexer head summation) and Metal sparse FA do not resolve it.

### Related
#27856 (HIP: depth-decay only, output correct), #28734 (CUDA: dense top-k TODO), #25722 (Metal: degenerate-token silent empty output, different arch), #21450 (Metal mixed KV rejection — the mechanism that pushes attention to CPU and avoids this bug)

*Disclosure: issue text prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode), verified against server logs and raw probe JSONs.*

title: Eval bug: draft-mtp draft context is sized from llama_n_ctx() (total) rather than llama_n_ctx_seq(), killing the server at decode entry on large --ctx-size
body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: b10752 (b96806d96)
```
Container image `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan`, run in router mode
(`--models-preset`), one child `llama-server` per model.

### Operating systems

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (Mesa RADV)

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 — Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO, gfx1151),
120 GiB GTT, unified memory.

### Models

`Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (dense, 27.3B params, `n_ctx_train = 262144`), which
carries MTP layers.

### Problem description

With `--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp` and a large `--ctx-size`, the server
fails **every** request — including a 13-token prompt — dying within ~2s of the
prompt/decode transition and exiting with status 1. The router respawns it, so
the failure presents as a ~53s crash-loop that silently discards all prompt
cache.

The trigger is the **total** `--ctx-size`, not the per-sequence context. That
appears to come from `common/speculative.cpp`, where the MTP draft context is
sized from the target's total context despite the comment stating per-sequence
intent:

```c
// common/speculative.cpp — common_speculative_init_result::common_speculative_init_result()
    auto cparams = common_context_params_to_llama(params);

    if (spec_mtp) {
        cparams.ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP;
    }

    // the draft context holds as many tokens per sequence as the target context
    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);        // <-- total, not per-sequence
```

`llama_n_ctx()` returns the total; `llama_n_ctx_seq()` is the per-sequence
accessor:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
uint32_t llama_n_ctx    (const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx();     }
uint32_t llama_n_ctx_seq(const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx_seq(); }
```

The draft context then builds its own memory module from those cparams:

```c
    memory.reset(model.create_memory(params_mem, cparams));
```

Under `--no-kv-unified` this makes the draft context `n_parallel` times larger
than the comment intends. Under `--kv-unified` it is worse, because
`n_ctx_seq` is then set equal to the whole total:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
    if (cparams.kv_unified) { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;                 }
    else                    { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / n_seq_max;     }
```

Note also that `--kv-unified-per-slot` cannot bound this: `llama_context_params`
has `n_ctx`, `n_seq_max` and `kv_unified`, but no per-slot field, so the
server-level cap never reaches the draft context.

### Ablation matrix

All rows below are on the same build, model, and machine, and each was verified
by serving requests. "draft n_ctx" is the value the code above assigns.

| `--ctx-size` | `--parallel` | kv-unified | `--spec-type` | draft `n_ctx` | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 786432 | **fails every request** |
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod` | — | works (12.8 tok/s, 99.99% cache reuse) |
| 393216 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 393216 | works (24 tok/s) |
| 524288 | 3 | on + `--kv-unified-per-slot 262144` | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 524288 | works (23.7 tok/s) |

Removing `draft-mtp` at the failing `--ctx-size` fixes it outright; restoring
`draft-mtp` at a smaller `--ctx-size` also fixes it. So the fault requires
`draft-mtp` **and** a large total `--ctx-size` together.

Note the third and fourth rows: the working unified config has a draft
`n_ctx_seq` of 524288, larger than the failing split config's 262144. So
per-sequence size is not the trigger — the **total** is.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 786432 --parallel 3 --no-kv-unified \
  --spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 4 --spec-draft-n-min 0 --draft-p-min 0.25 \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 --flash-attn on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --jinja

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"...","max_tokens":8,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say: ok"}]}'
```

The model loads normally and reports `status=loaded`. The first request — any
size — kills the process.

### What was ruled out

- **GPU/driver watchdog.** This machine separately had `amdgpu.lockup_timeout`
  at its 2000 ms default, which produced `ring comp_1.x.1 timeout`, a compute
  queue reset and `vk::DeviceLostError`. That was raised to
  `10000,60000,10000,10000` and the machine rebooted. `dmesg` has shown **zero**
  ring timeouts since, yet the MTP failure persists — so the two are unrelated
  faults and this report is only about the second.
- **Out of memory.** The failing configuration loads cleanly at 82 GiB of 120
  GiB GTT, and no OOM appears in `dmesg`. The failure is on first use, not at
  allocation.
- **Prompt length.** A 13-token prompt fails identically to a 100k one.
- **Tool/grammar constrained sampling.** A request with no `tools` fails too.
- **Build drift.** `b10752-b96806d96` throughout, verified via
  `system_fingerprint`; the container was restarted, never re-pulled.
- **Slot count alone.** `--parallel 3` works fine at smaller `--ctx-size`.

### Suggested fix

```diff
-    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);
+    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx_seq(ctx_tgt);
```

This matches the stated intent of the comment. It would also make the draft
context independent of `--parallel`, which currently multiplies it.

### Possibly related

#23658 reports MTP draft acceptance collapsing at particular `--ctx-size`
values on a ~2048-aligned pattern, attributed there to "slot indexing in how
the MTP draft context shares the KV cache with the target context". That may be
the same sizing/indexing surface presenting as degradation rather than a crash.

### Relevant log output

```

I srv    operator(): instance name=coder-senior exited with status 1
W srv    operator(): got exception: {"error":{"code":500,"message":"request cancelled while waiting for model name=coder-senior","type":"server_error"}}

# after raising it, the child exits 1 with no exception text and no kernel event
```

title: Misc. bug: uncaught integer overflows during model loading
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.5.0-dev (build 709, commit 70596c4)
built with Clang 14.0.6 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server, llama-cli

### Command line

```shell
llama-cli -m bug_model.gguf
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

While fuzzing llama.cpp, I found several uncaught integer overflows during tensor parsing.

First one is improper int-overflow guard at gguf_init_from_reader(). The existing validation attempts
to ensure that the total number of elements is representable:
```
if (ok && ggml_nelements(&info.t) > 0 &&
    ((INT64_MAX/info.t.ne[1] <= info.t.ne[0]) ||
     (INT64_MAX/info.t.ne[2] <= info.t.ne[0]*info.t.ne[1]) ||
     (INT64_MAX/info.t.ne[3] <= info.t.ne[0]*info.t.ne[1]*info.t.ne[2]))) {
    ...
}
```

However, the arithmetic performed by the validation itself can overflow in `ggml_nelements()`, before result is checked. Additionally,
if one of the elements is zero (or multiplication overflows to zero), the condition becomes false and validation skipped entirely.
 
Another one is missing guard for possible integer overflows in ggml_new_tensor_impl(), that cause many overflow errors in ggml.c.
One of the UBSAN reports:

title: Feature Request: split generation timings into reasoning and answer phases (rate and draft acceptance per phase)
body:
### Prerequisites

- [ ] I am running the latest code. Development is rapid so there are no tagged versions as of now. (Tested on the latest release, **v0.5.0**, b11146, commit 7fe450e19; the relevant server code is unchanged on master as of 2026-09-24.)
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Split the generation timings of a reasoning model into its two phases, reasoning and answer, in `llama-server`'s `timings` and in the `print_timing` log line.

Today `timings` reports one `predicted_n` / `predicted_ms` / `predicted_per_second`, plus one `draft_n` / `draft_n_accepted`, for the whole completion. With a reasoning model and speculative decoding those numbers average two workloads that behave very differently, so the single figure describes neither.

Proposed shape (names are only a suggestion), added next to the existing fields and emitted only when the response actually contained reasoning:

```json
"timings": {
  "predicted_n": 2048, "predicted_ms": 71416.1, "predicted_per_second": 28.66,
  "draft_n": 1902, "draft_n_accepted": 1412,
  "reasoning": {
    "predicted_n": 1825, "predicted_ms": 65216.3,
    "draft_n": 1737, "draft_n_accepted": 1247
  }
}
```

The answer phase is then the difference, so one extra object is enough. The `print_timing` line at the end of a request could carry the same split (`reasoning: 1825 tokens, 28.0 t/s, acc 72% | answer: 223 tokens, 35.6 t/s, acc 100%`).

### Motivation

We tune `--spec-draft-n-max` and pick quants from benchmarks, and a reasoning model's mean decode rate is the wrong number to tune on: how much of the output is reasoning moves with the question, and in agentic coding the reasoning phase is usually most of it.

Measured on llama.cpp v0.5.0 (b11146), Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on an R9700 (ROCm) + RTX 4070 SUPER (CUDA) split, DFlash2 drafter, `temperature 0`, 2048 output tokens, 93.6k-token prompt, 3 repetitions each (the split was obtained client-side, see below):

| drafter | reasoning t/s | reasoning acc | answer t/s | answer acc | whole request t/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 13.0 | | 12.9 | | 13.0 |
| DFlash2, n-max 3 | 28.0 (1825 tok) | 72% | 35.6 (223 tok) | 100% | 28.7 |
| DFlash2, n-max 7 | 33.7 (2048 tok) | 51% | (not reached) | | 33.6 |

- The answer drafts at 100% acceptance and is capped by `n-max` itself; the reasoning drafts at 51 to 72%. Their mean is a regime that does not exist.
- The phase share also changes between otherwise identical runs: at `temperature 0` the n-max 5 and 7 runs reasoned past the 2048-token cap while n-max 3 answered at token 1825, so two "decode" means compared naively mix different phase proportions.
- In the server log the phase change is visible as a step in `tg_3s` (about 22 t/s during reasoning, about 40 t/s once the answer starts, on a request with a longer answer), but nothing in the timings says where it happened.

The count alone (#27971, `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, closed by its author) would not be enough for this: the rate and the draft acceptance per phase need the time and the draft counters at the boundary.

### Possible Implementation

We currently get this client-side: stream with `"timings_per_token": true`, and read the cumulative `timings` on the last event whose delta is `reasoning_content`; each phase is a difference of the server's own counters, with no client clock. That works, but it needs streaming and per-token timings on every event, and any client that does not stream cannot get it.

Server-side, the boundary is already known at generation time in two places:

- `task_result_state::update_chat_msg` (tools/server/server-task.cpp) separates `reasoning_content` from `content` incrementally while streaming;
- the `reasoning-budget` sampler (common/reasoning-budget.cpp) tracks the reasoning block token by token (`REASONING_BUDGET_COUNTING` to `REASONING_BUDGET_DONE`), but only when a budget is set.

A snapshot of `server_slot_stats` (`n_gen`, `t_gen_last`, `n_draft_tokens`, `n_draft_accepted`) taken when the first non-reasoning token is emitted would give the `reasoning` object above; tokens of one speculative step share one timestamp, so step granularity is the natural precision.

Happy to test a PR on ROCm (gfx1201) + CUDA.

title: CUDA flash attention inefficiency in quantized KV cache handling, worsening with context length
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

The stock CUDA MMA fa path supports f16 KV tiles only, thus any quantized KV that flows through it must be converted to f16 first, which is currently being done via a scratch buffer. This introduces a performance hit that gets more expensive as context length increases. Add specialized per-quant-type handling to the CUDA MMA fa path, obviating the need for its scratch buffer.

Related:
- #24166 & #23978: Stock implementation details
- #27109: Performance issues for q4 specifically
- #27623: Decode performance degradation in long contexts

Version:
53ed051c

### Motivation

With GPUs as prohibitively expensive as they currently are, people running cards just one generation behind (and older) either have to live with a tradeoff between:
- Slower decode
- Smaller context windows
- Not being able to fit the whole model in VRAM at all

Our lab has a 4090 and two 8000s, so we feel this pain.

The q8/q4 quants fit our selfish use case, so we start with those.

### Possible Implementation

Add specialized per-quant-type handling to the CUDA MMA fa path, obviating the need for its scratch buffer.
